docs.title: arena-interface
docs.text:
A Python library for controlling the G6 arena controller (Teensy 4.1) over its USB serial connection. It replaces the JavaScript host library with a blocking, fully type-hinted Python API for scripts and notebooks.

from arena_interface import Device, TrialMode

with Device.open() as dev:                      # finds the controller by USB id
    print(dev.firmware_version)                 # e.g. "12bba7e9 2x10 2026-11-02 main"
    dev.start_trial(1, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=60, duration=5)

docs.title: What it covers
docs.text:
• Every firmware command: display control, trials from the SD card, host-chosen frames, streamed frames, the SD pattern library, analog and digital I/O, health and crash diagnostics, the telemetry log, and panel firmware updates.
  • Patterns from pixel arrays: build .pat files and stream frames from numpy arrays or nested lists, for any arena preset or custom grid. The output matches the JavaScript tools byte for byte.
  • Host-paced playback: play frame sequences at a fixed rate (SD frames or streamed images), blocking, in the background, or live, with a timing report.
  • Continuous data: an event stream of what the arena actually displayed, timed by the controller, and fixed-rate sampling of any reading.
  • Safety: closing a connection blanks the arena; commands the firmware does not support, or that would stop the display because of a bad argument, are refused before anything is sent.
  • A simulated controller that behaves like the firmware, so tests, examples and notebooks run without hardware.

docs.text:

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer on Linux, macOS or Windows.
  • pyserial and numpy, installed automatically.
  • Optional: matplotlib (plotting example), OpenCV (webcam and movie examples, the camera extra), Jupyter (notebook example).

docs.title: Wire Protocol
docs.text:
This page describes the USB-serial protocol spoken by the G6 arena controller firmware (Teensy 4.1). It was derived from reference/firmware/ (the source of truth) and cross-checked against the JavaScript host in reference/js/. The panel firmware in reference/panel/ is the authority on how pixel bytes inside a panel block are displayed. Source locations are given as File:line where useful.

All multi-byte integers are little-endian. "u8/u16/u32/i16" are unsigned / signed integer widths. Opcodes are written in hex.

docs.title: Serial settings
docs.text:
Setting Value Transport USB CDC-ACM (Teensy 4.1 native USB, Serial) Baud rate Ignored by USB CDC. Firmware calls Serial.begin(115200); the host may open at any rate (use 115200 by convention). Data bits / parity / stop Irrelevant on USB CDC (8N1 by convention). Flow control None. USB VID/PID 16C0:0483 (PJRC "Teensyduino Serial", the stock Teensy USB-serial IDs; confirmed with lsusb on a real controller). These identify any Teensy in serial mode, not specifically this controller. Ethernet The firmware also has a TCP path (port 62222) with identical framing, but net.begin()/serviceTcp() are commented out in main.cpp. Out of scope for this library.

Only one process can hold the port at a time.

docs.title: Arena variants
docs.text:
One firmware image targets exactly one arena geometry, chosen at build time (constants.h:47-59). The host learns it from GET_FIRMWARE_VERSION (rows, cols).

Build flag Rows × cols Panels Stream frame GS2 / GS16 (bytes) Default refresh GS16 / GS2 (Hz) ARENA_HW_2_10 2 × 10 20 1064 / 4064 300 / 1000 ARENA_HW_10_10 4 × 10 40 2124 / 8124 400 / 1200 ARENA_HW_12_18 4 × 12 48 2548 / 9748 400 / 1200

Stream frame size = 4 + panels × block, with block = 53 B (GS2) or 203 B (GS16).

docs.title: Message framing
docs.text: The link is a raw byte stream; there are no delimiters or checksums at the USB level. Framing is decided by the first byte of each host message (SerialManager.cpp:parseIncoming).

docs.title: Host → device
docs.text:
First byte Form Layout 0x00–0x31 Binary command [len, cmd, params…] — len = number of bytes after it (1 + params). Max len is 0x31, i.e. at most 48 parameter bytes. 0x32 Stream frame [0x32, len_lo, len_hi, payload…] — len = payload byte count (u16). 0x83 Rename (opcode-first) [0x83, idx u16, name_len u8, name…] — name_len 1–63. 0x85 Pattern upload (bulk) [0x85, idx u16, size u64, data…] — 11-byte header then size raw bytes. 0xE0 Firmware upload (bulk) [0xE0, size u64, data…] — 9-byte header then size raw bytes. anything else — The device discards its whole receive buffer to resync. No reply.

Notes:

  • The binary length byte doubles as the discriminator, which is why commands that may exceed 48 parameter bytes use opcode-first framing.
  • Only the low 32 bits of the u64 size fields are used (SerialManager.cpp:105,133).
  • SET_PATTERN_FILENAME (0x83) is accepted in both binary framing (when it fits) and opcode-first framing. The library should always use opcode-first.
  • A stream frame whose claimed length exceeds the receive buffer, or a 0x83 frame with name_len 0 or ≥ 64, makes the device silently discard its receive buffer. No reply is sent; the host sees a timeout.

docs.title: Device → host: response frame
docs.text:
Every dispatched command produces exactly one response frame:

[len, status, echo_cmd, payload…]
  • len = bytes after it (2 + payload). Response buffer is 200 bytes, so the payload is at most 196 bytes and len ≤ 198. If a handler's payload would not fit, the payload is silently dropped and only [2, status, echo] is sent (SerialManager.cpp:sendResponse). No current handler hits this.
  • status = 0 on success, non-zero on failure (see Error handling).
  • echo_cmd = the request opcode (0x32 for stream frames).
  • payload = either raw binary fields (GET-style commands) or an ASCII message without a NUL terminator (MessageSource.h:sendResponse(const char*) uses strlen). An empty message ("") produces no payload.

There is no request id. Correlation is by echo_cmd, so the host must keep one request in flight at a time (see Concurrency).

docs.title: Device → host: bulk data
docs.text: GET_PATTERN_FILE (0x84) and GET_SD_ARCHIVE (0x8A) send a normal response frame whose payload is a u64 size (status 0), followed immediately by size raw bytes with no framing. If the transfer aborts (host stalls > 2 s, SD read error, 60 s idle) the device just stops sending; there is no trailer or error frame. The host detects failure by receiving fewer than size bytes.

docs.title: Device → host: diagnostic text (DEBUG_SERIAL builds only)
docs.text: Debug builds can interleave text lines on the same pipe. Each line starts with the sentinel byte 0xFF and ends with \n (constants.h:diag_line_sentinel, main.cpp:SentinelPrint). 0xFF can never be a response length byte (max 198), so the host can demultiplex: a frame that begins with 0xFF is a diagnostic line to be read up to \n. Diagnostics are off at boot and controlled by SET_DIAG_OUTPUT (0xC3); boot-time banner lines are printed unconditionally in debug builds. Release builds never emit them. The flag bit GET_FIRMWARE_VERSION.flags bit1 tells the host whether it is a debug build.

docs.title: Device state
docs.text:
The controller is always in one of these states (CommandProcessor.h:ArenaState; reported as GET_HEALTH.state):

Value State Entered by 0 ALL_OFF boot, 0x00, 0x30, trial duration expiry, end of error glyph, bad stream size 1 ALL_ON 0xFF 2 STREAMING_FRAME 0x32 3 OPEN_LOOP (mode 2) 0x08 mode 2 4 SHOW_FRAME (mode 3) 0x08 mode 3, 0x03, 0x70 5 CLOSED_LOOP (mode 4) 0x08 mode 4 6 PSRAM_PLAY 0x3A, 0x3B 7 ERROR_DISPLAY many errors (see below); auto-returns to ALL_OFF after 750 ms

Entering ALL_OFF sends a dark frame three times so the panels actually blank (panels hold their last frame otherwise).

Several commands are refused unless the state is ALL_OFF (status 10, CE_DISPLAY_ACTIVE), and several are refused while an SD transfer (0x84 / 0x85 / 0x8A) is running (status 1, "SD transfer in progress").

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Request bytes are shown for binary framing ([len, cmd, …]). "Reply" lists the success payload; on failure the payload is an ASCII message unless noted.

GS16, all pixels max. 30 STOP_DISPLAY 01 30 "Display has been stopped" Same effect as ALL_OFF. 08 TRIAL_PARAMS 0C 08 mode pat:u16 rate:i16 init:u16 gain:i16 dur:u16 (+ duty:u8 → 0D) empty Start mode 2/3/4 with 1-based SD pattern. rate Hz (mode 2; negative = reverse). init 0-based start frame (taken modulo frame count). gain = 10× fps/V (mode 4). dur in 10 ms ticks, 0 = run until stopped. duty 0 = pattern's stored duty, 1–255 = override for this trial. Errors: < 11 params, mode ∉ {2,3,4}, or pattern load failure → error glyph + status 1. C6 GET_SPI_CLOCK 01 C6 mhz:u16

docs.title: SD card / pattern library
docs.text:
Patterns are /patterns/*.pat, sorted alphabetically, addressed by a 1-based index (max 256 listed). Index 0 means the staging file /patterns/pattern.temp where noted. Renames and deletes re-sort / compact the index space.

Op Name Request Reply payload Notes 80 GET_FILE_COUNT 01 80 count:u16 82 GET_PATTERN_FILENAME 03 82 idx:u16 name_len:u8, name Status 1 "Index out of range". 88 GET_PATTERN_INFO 03 88 idx:u16 frame_count:u16, gs:u8, rows:u8, cols:u8, arena_id:u8, observer_id:u8, file_size:u32, duty_cycle:u8 (12 B) gs 1 = GS2, 2 = GS16. duty_cycle = frame 0 / panel 0. Allowed while displaying. Failure status = CE code. 83 SET_PATTERN_FILENAME 83 idx:u16 name_len:u8 name new_idx:u16 Rename; idx 0 promotes pattern.temp. name_len 1–63. Refused during SD transfer. Failure status = CE code. 84 GET_PATTERN_FILE 03 84 idx:u16 size:u64, then size raw bytes Requires ALL_OFF. See bulk data. 85 SET_PATTERN_FILE 85 idx:u16 size:u64 data empty, sent after all data is received idx 0 writes pattern.temp, idx ≥ 1 overwrites that pattern. Requires ALL_OFF. size 0 → immediate status 1. On any other rejection the device still reads and discards all size bytes before replying. Idle timeout 30 s. 86 DELETE_PATTERN_FILE 03 86 idx:u16 empty idx 0 deletes pattern.temp. Failure status = CE code. 8F PURGE_MEMORY 01 8F empty Formats the whole SD card (patterns, panel firmware, manifests). Requires ALL_OFF and no transfer. Slow (scales with card size). 8A GET_SD_ARCHIVE 01 8A size:u64, then a ZIP (store mode) Requires ALL_OFF. Contains MANIFEST.bin, MANIFEST.txt and patterns/*.pat. CD GET_SD_INFO 01 CD 30 B: ver, flags, card_type, fat_type, sectors:u32, bytes_per_cluster:u32, cid[16], sd_status_maint, sd_diag Status 1 still carries the payload (no card mounted). CE SET_SD_DIAG 02 CE flags flags:u8 Bench switches: bit0 legacy seek, bit1 no same-index skip. Bits 2–7 must be 0.

docs.text: Op Name Request Reply payload Notes A0 SET_AO_VOLTAGE 03 A0 mv:u16 mv:u16 0–5000 mV on the analog-out BNC. Stops LUT playback. Refused in AO mode 1. A1 GET_AO_VOLTAGE 01 A1 mv:u16 Read back from the DAC (12-bit quantized), not the commanded value. A2 SET_AO_LUT len A2 mode step_hz:u16 count:u16 mv:u16×count count:u16 mode 0 = frame-locked, 1 = time-based at step_hz (≤ 1000). Each mv 0–5000. count ≤ 21 (binary framing limit, see Quirks). Refused in AO mode 1. A3 SET_AO_MODE 02 A3 mode empty 0 programmable, 1 frame_number (DAC tracks frame index, 0–5 V across the pattern). A4 GET_ANALOG_IN 01 A4 ain1_mv:i16, ain2_mv:i16 ±10 V inputs, 10-bit ADC, uncalibrated. AA SET_DIGITAL_OUT 03 AA channel state empty channel 1/2; state 0/non-zero. A port in role off is auto-promoted to out_programmable; a port in in_trigger or out_debug_framescan is refused (status 1). AB GET_DIGITAL_OUT 01 AB level1:u8, level2:u8 Live pin reads. AC SET_DIO_ROLE 03 AC port role empty port 1/2; role 0 off, 1 in_trigger, 2 out_programmable, 3 out_debug_framescan. Boot defaults: port 1 = out_programmable (LOW), port 2 = in_trigger. AD GET_DIO_ROLE 01 AD role1, level1, role2, level2

docs.title: Identity, health and diagnostics
docs.text: Op Name Request Reply payload Notes C2 GET_CONTROLLER_INFO 01 C2 version:u8, capability:u8, mac[6] version = 1. This firmware reports capability 0xA3. See capability bits. CB GET_FIRMWARE_VERSION 01 CB 46 B: ver, rows, cols, flags, sha[8], date[10], branch[24] ASCII fields right-padded with spaces. Gated by capability bit 7. CA GET_HEALTH 01 CA 114 B (ver = 5) Cumulative counters, previous-boot breadcrumb, watchdog state. Layout in CommandProcessor.cpp:1078-1128; offsets never move between versions. Gated by capability bit 7. CC GET_CRASHREPORT 01 CC 128 B raw PJRC arm_fault_info_struct (44 B) + PJRC breadcrumbs. Not cleared by reading. Gated by firmware flags bit 3. A8 SET_TELEMETRY 02 A8 flags or 04 A8 flags rate:u16 empty bit0 record events (on at boot); bit7 synthetic producer at rate/s; bit4 = watchdog bits present, then bit6 watchdog off, bit5 starve watchdog (resets the controller after 2 s). Gated by firmware flags bit 2. A9 GET_TELEMETRY_BLOCK 08 A9 ack_seq:u32 max_bytes:u16 flags 18-byte header + whole records Frees records with seq ≤ ack_seq (0xFFFFFFFF = no ack), then returns up to min(max_bytes, 178) bytes of records without freeing them. Record format below. C1 GET_ETHERNET_IP_ADDRESS 01 C1 ASCII dotted quad Ethernet is not started in this build, so the value is not meaningful. C3 SET_DIAG_OUTPUT 02 C3 on (or 01 C3 = on) "diag on" / "diag off" Only has an effect on DEBUG_SERIAL builds. C4 GET_DIAG_OUTPUT 01 C4 on:u8 01 SYSTEM_RESET 01 01 "rebooting" Replies, then resets ~10 ms later. USB drops and re-enumerates.

docs.title: Panel firmware (in-system programming)
docs.text: Op Name Request Reply payload Notes E0 SET_FIRMWARE_FILE E0 size:u64 data crc32:u32 (CRC-32/ISO-HDLC of stored bytes) Writes /firmware/panel.bin. Requires ALL_OFF and no transfer. Blocking; idle timeout 30 s. E3 GET_FIRMWARE_INFO 01 E3 32 B footer: magic[8], version[16], crc32:u32, size:u32 Status 1 if no image. C8 G6_PROGRAM_PANEL 02 C8 panel_number ASCII result message 1-based panel number. Requires ALL_OFF. Blocks for several seconds. C9 G6_VERIFY_PANEL 02 C9 panel_number ASCII result message Status 0 = CRC match. Requires ALL_OFF.

docs.title: Reserved / rejected opcodes
docs.text: 06 SWITCH_GRAYSCALE replies status 1 with an explanation (dropped for G6). C0, C7, 71, 73 are defined in commands.h but not implemented. They, and every other unknown opcode, are handled as an unknown command: the arena shows a "CE 01" error glyph for 750 ms (which stops any running display) and the reply is status 1 "Unknown command". Hosts must therefore not probe for optional commands; they must gate on the capability/feature flags below.

docs.title: Capability and feature flags
docs.text:
GET_CONTROLLER_INFO.capability (constants.h:187):

Bit Name Meaning 0 g6_mode Always 1 on G6 1 v2_local_storage 2 mode_1_tsi 3 v3_triggered 4 v3_gated 5 io_ext 0xA3, 0xA4, 0xAC, 0xAD present 6 ai_cal (claimed by a different firmware branch; not set here) 7 health 0xCA and 0xCB present

GET_FIRMWARE_VERSION.flags (Version.h):

Bit Meaning Gates 0 Dirty working tree at build — 1 DEBUG_SERIAL build (diagnostic text may appear) — 2 Telemetry ring present 0xA8, 0xA9 3 Crash report + health v2 present 0xCC 4 Free-running refresh timer — 5 SD fast path 0xCD 6 SD diagnostics 0xCE

docs.title: Pattern file format (.pat)
docs.text: Patterns on the SD card (and uploaded with 0x85) use the G6 v2 format. The layout below is what the firmware validates (SdManager.cpp:validateHeader, readFrame) and what reference/js/pat-encoder.js / pat-parser.js write and read. The firmware passes panel blocks to the panels unchanged, apart from the display-mode bits and an optional per-trial duty override.

docs.title: Header (18 bytes)
docs.text:
Offset Field 0–3 Magic "G6PT" 4 bits 7–4: format version (must be 2); bits 3–0: arena_id bits 5–2 5 bits 7–6: arena_id bits 1–0; bits 5–0: observer_id 6–7 frame_count:u16 (must be > 0) 8 panel rows 9 panel cols 10 gs: 1 = GS2 (on/off), 2 = GS16 (16 levels) 11–16 panel mask, 48 bits, bit i = panel i (byte 11 bit 0 = panel 0) 17 CRC-8/AUTOSAR over bytes 0–16 (poly 0x2F, init 0xFF, xorout 0xFF, not reflected; check "123456789" → 0xDF)

The firmware rejects a file unless rows × cols equals this build's arena (CE_ARENA_MISMATCH), the mask has at most rows × cols bits set, and the magic, version, CRC-8, frame count and gs are valid (CE_HEADER_CRC). arena_id and observer_id are host metadata only. The JS parser also reads an older 17-byte v1 header; the firmware does not accept v1.

docs.title: Frames
docs.text:
frame_count frames follow the header back to back. Each frame is:

Part Size Content Prefix 4 'F','R', frame_index:u16 Panel blocks panels × 53 (GS2) or × 203 (GS16) One block per panel, row-major, panel row 0 = bottom of the arena Trailer 2 CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE (poly 0x1021, init 0xFFFF, no xorout; check → 0x29B1) over prefix + blocks, little-endian

The firmware checks the "FR" magic and the CRC-16 of every frame it displays (CE_FRAME_CRC). It does not check frame_index.

A stream frame payload (0x32) is exactly one frame without its trailer.

docs.title: Panel block
docs.text:
Offset GS2 (53 B) GS16 (203 B) 0 header: bits 6–0 = protocol version 1, bit 7 = even parity same 1 display opcode 0x10 (written as oneshot) 0x30 2… 50 bytes, 1 bit/pixel, MSB first 200 bytes, 4 bits/pixel, even pixel in high nibble last duty_cycle (brightness 0–255; 0 = off) same
  • Parity: bit 7 of byte 0 is chosen so the number of 1 bits in {byte 0 bits 6–0, all following bytes} is even (G6PanelProtocol.h:stamp_header_parity).
  • Opcode: the low 2 bits (display mode) are rewritten by the firmware at display time from SET_PANEL_DISPLAY_MODE, so the file value does not matter.
  • Duty: the JS encoder writes 128 by default. A trial's duty parameter (0x08) overrides it at display time.
  • Pixel order: row-major, starting at the top row of the panel: pixel = row_from_top × 20 + col, col 0 = left. This is what the panel firmware does (reference/panel/message.cpp:to_pattern_gray_2/16 unpacks pixel n into matrix row n / 20; isp_logic.h:74 states "Row 0 = top" for the matrix, and its built-in ERR and smiley glyphs read upright with that convention). The .pat encoder in pat-encoder.js follows it too. Confirmed on hardware: the controller's error glyph, which is packed bottom row first, shows on the panels upside down with the digits above "CE". Across the arena, panel blocks are in row-major order starting from the bottom row of panels, columns left to right, so block k is panel number k + 1 (as used by PROGRAM_PANEL / VERIFY_PANEL). A host image with row 0 at the bottom must therefore flip rows within each panel when packing. Confirmed on hardware (2×10 build, panels 4 and 5 fitted, 2026-11-04): the image's bottom panel row, column 3 lit panel 4; the top panel row lit nothing; the top-left 6×6 pixels of each panel lit the top-left corner of panels 4 and 5; panel 4 is left of panel 5.

docs.title: Telemetry records
docs.text:
GET_TELEMETRY_BLOCK reply header (18 B): t_now_us:u32, first_seq:u32, n_records:u16, dropped:u32, more:u8, flags:u8, boot_count:u16. Header flags: bit0 events enabled, bit1 ring survived a reboot, bit2 ring disabled (heap collision), bit3 synthetic producer on.

Records follow back to back (Telemetry.h):

Offset Field 0 len:u8 (whole record) 1 type:u8 — 1 CMD, 2 FRAME, 3 STATE (0 PAD is never returned) 2 seq:u32 6 t_us:u32 (raw micros(); wraps every ~71.6 min) 10 type-specific payload
  • CMD (13–21 B): cmd:u8, status:u8, plen:u8, request_bytes[plen ≤ 8].
  • FRAME (26 B): idx:u16, pattern:u16, sd_load_us:u32, spi_us:u16, req_age_us:u32, superseded:u8, flags:u8.
  • STATE (14 B): kind:u8, code:u8, arg:u16; kinds 1–14 as listed in Telemetry.h:118-145.

The intended drain loop: send ack_seq = 0xFFFFFFFF first, then ack_seq = first_seq + n_records - 1 of the last block received, repeating while more is 1. A lost reply is recovered by resending the same ack.

docs.title: Asynchronous messages
docs.text:
None. The firmware never sends unsolicited frames. Every frame is a reply to a command, except:

  • raw bulk bytes after a 0x84 / 0x8A header (solicited), and
  • 0xFF-prefixed diagnostic text lines on DEBUG_SERIAL builds.

Anything "streamed" from the device (frame position, analog inputs, health, telemetry events) must be polled by the host. The telemetry ring is the designed mechanism for a complete event log (commands, frame changes, state changes) with no gaps.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text:
Status Name Typical source 0 OK 1 generic error / CE_UNKNOWN_CMD Most validation failures (message in payload); unknown opcode 2 CE_BAD_PAYLOAD_LEN (used as glyph code; replies use 1) 3 CE_BAD_PARAM Index out of range (SD manager) 4 CE_SD_NOT_PRESENT No SD card 5 CE_SD_FILE_ERROR File missing / unreadable / rename or delete failed 6 CE_HEADER_CRC Bad pattern header (magic, version, CRC-8) 7 CE_FRAME_CRC Bad frame CRC-16 8 CE_ARENA_MISMATCH Pattern geometry ≠ this arena 9 CE_MANIFEST_WRITE_ERROR Manifest update failed 10 CE_DISPLAY_ACTIVE Command needs ALL_OFF 11 CE_SD_FORMAT_ERROR Purge (format) failed

Codes 2–11 appear as reply statuses only from the SD handlers (0x83, 0x86, 0x88, 0x8F) and from CE_DISPLAY_ACTIVE guards. Display-start failures (0x08, 0x03, 0x70) always reply status 1, but show the precise CE code as a glyph on the arena. The ASCII payload is the only way to tell status-1 errors apart.

docs.title: Error glyph side effect
docs.text: These failures put the arena into ERROR_DISPLAY ("CE NN" on every panel) for 750 ms, then ALL_OFF, stopping whatever was being displayed: unknown opcodes; TRIAL_PARAMS too short / bad mode / load failure; SET_PATTERN_ID load failure; SET_FRAME_POSITION with no pattern, index out of range, or read failure; DISPLAY_PSRAM_INDEX / PSRAM_PLAY too short. The library should validate arguments locally so that these are not triggered by host bugs.

docs.title: Malformed input
docs.text: Input Device behaviour Unknown first byte Receive buffer discarded, no reply → host timeout Stream frame too large for buffer Receive buffer discarded, no reply Stream frame of wrong (but bufferable) size ALL_OFF, status 1 0x83 with name_len 0 or ≥ 64 (opcode-first) Receive buffer discarded, no reply Binary command with wrong parameter count Status 1 with "Expected […]" message (per handler)

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text: After a timeout, stale bytes may still arrive. The host should discard its receive buffer (the JS host does this) before sending the next request.

docs.text: Item Value Source Normal command reply well under 1 ms of device time; JS uses a 500 ms timeout arena-link.js:70 PURGE_MEMORY (0x8F) tens of seconds to minutes (SD format); JS uses 120 s arena-wire-g6.js:583 G6_PROGRAM_PANEL / VERIFY (0xC8/0xC9) several seconds CommandProcessor.cpp:2729 GET_SD_ARCHIVE (0x8A) header proportional to file count (stat of up to 258 files) Bulk download (0x84/0x8A) device aborts after 2 s with no host read progress, or 60 s idle SerialManager.cpp:sendRaw Bulk upload (0x85) 30 s idle → abort and drain (≤ 5 s more), then status 1 CommandProcessor.h:259 Rejected bulk upload device drains: 5 s idle / 15 s absolute CommandProcessor.cpp:drainBulkData Firmware upload (0xE0) 30 s idle SYSTEM_RESET reply then reset after ~10 ms; USB re-enumerates (~1–3 s) Boot panels blanked at boot and again 3.5 s after reset constants.h:panel_late_boot_blank_ms Error glyph hold 750 ms, then ALL_OFF constants.h:error_display_hold_ms Trial duration tick 10 ms constants.h:duration_tick_ms Mode 4 AIN sampling 500 Hz Hardware watchdog 2 s (30 s during long ops) — a wedged controller resets itself Health.h

docs.title: Refresh rate and measured performance
docs.text:
The refresh rate is how often the controller re-sends the current frame to all panels over SPI (a timer in the controller firmware). A new frame reaches the panels at the next refresh tick. Defaults (constants.h): 2x10 builds 300 Hz for GS16 content and 1000 Hz for GS2; other builds 400 / 1200 Hz. The controller switches between the GS2 and GS16 defaults automatically, until the host sets a rate with SET_REFRESH_RATE: that rate then applies to all content until the controller reboots. Separately, each panel scans its LEDs at a fixed 1 kHz (reference/panel/display.cpp), which is not adjustable from the host; frame rates above 1 kHz bring no visible benefit.

Measured on a 2x10 controller (firmware 12bba7e9, debug build, 25 MHz SPI, Linux host in a VM, 2026-11-05). No panel errors were seen at any rate.

Refresh (set) GS16 transfers achieved GS2 transfers achieved 300-1250 Hz as set as set 1500 Hz 1282/s (SPI saturated) as set up to 3000 Hz — as set

Host-paced frames, sent as fast as possible ("shown" = distinct frames that reached the panels; for streamed frames, at most min(sends, transfers)):

Method Refresh Commands/s Frames shown/s SET_FRAME_POSITION (SD, GS16) 300 Hz 571 298 500 Hz 478 473 1000 Hz 353 352 STREAM_FRAME GS16 (4064 B) 300 Hz 1107 ≤ 300 1000 Hz 951 ≤ 951 1250 Hz 415 ≤ 415 STREAM_FRAME GS2 (1064 B) 1000 Hz 2340 ≤ 1000

Each refresh transfer blocks the controller's main loop (about 0.7 ms for a 2x10 GS16 frame), so higher refresh rates leave less time for commands; at 1250 Hz and above, GS16 transfers saturate SPI and command handling drops sharply. A streamed frame takes effect when it arrives, so it is displayed if the host sends frames no faster than the refresh rate (each frame then stays in place for at least one refresh period). An SD frame (SET_FRAME_POSITION) takes effect only after the controller has read it from the card, which usually takes about 1.7 ms but occasionally stalls; at fps close to the refresh rate a delayed frame can then be replaced before it is shown (seen once: 1 of 99 frames at 200 fps with a 300 Hz refresh). For SD playback that must show every frame, keep fps well below the refresh rate or raise the refresh rate, and check with play_frames(..., verify=True).

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text:
• The device parses one command at a time and has one response buffer. A response that the host has not drained yet can be overwritten by the next command's response. The host must wait for each reply before sending the next command (single flight).
  • During a bulk transfer the device does not process other commands on the serial link. The host must not send anything until the transfer completes.

docs.title: Quirks
docs.text:
1. Binary command length limit. Length byte must be ≤ 0x31, so a binary command carries at most 48 parameter bytes. SET_AO_LUT therefore accepts at most 21 entries per command, although the firmware buffer holds 4096 (CommandProcessor.cpp:938 checks only needed ≤ 255).
  2. Display keeps running after the host disconnects. USB CDC disconnect does not change the device state. A "safe" close must send ALL_OFF (see Host-side decisions).
  3. GET_SD_INFO returns its full payload with status 1 when no card is mounted.
  4. SET_REFRESH_RATE is sticky for the rest of the boot: after one explicit rate, the per-grayscale defaults are no longer applied.
  5. Index shifting. DELETE and RENAME re-sort the 1-based pattern indices; cached index → name maps must be refreshed afterwards.
  6. Patterns must match the arena. A pattern whose rows × cols differ from the firmware build is rejected (CE_ARENA_MISMATCH).
  7. Status 1 is overloaded. It means both "generic error" and CE_UNKNOWN_CMD; only the ASCII message distinguishes them.
  8. Bulk download failures are silent: the only signal is a short byte count.

docs.title: Discrepancies
docs.text:
Firmware and JS disagree in the places below. The library follows the firmware.

Sending them to this firmware would trigger a CE 01 glyph. SET_AO_LUT (0xA2), SET_PATTERN_ID (0x03), PSRAM (0x3A/0x3B) Implemented Not encoded Implement. GET_AO_VOLTAGE meaning DAC hardware readback (quantized) "last commanded level" Document as readback. GET_ANALOG_IN length 4 bytes Optional 5th flags byte Decode 4 bytes; tolerate a longer payload. GET_PATTERN_INFO byte 11 duty_cycle stretch Name it duty_cycle. GET_HEALTH size/version ver 5, 114 bytes (code); header comment still says ver 1 / 66 B Decodes 55 B base + tails up to v5 Decode by length like the JS, documenting v5. GET_CRASHREPORT gate flags bit 3 One comment says bit 2, another bit 3 Bit 3. SET_SD_DIAG gate flags bit 6 Comment says bit 5 Bit 6. GET_TELEMETRY_BLOCK max_bytes Capped at 178 Default 180 Default 178. SET_SPI_CLOCK range Clamps to 1–30, echoes applied Throws outside 1–30 Validate 1–30 locally (clearer errors); return the applied value. Comments on 0xC1/0xC2 encoders — Say 01 C0 / 01 C1 JS comment typos; opcodes are 0xC1 / 0xC2. Stream frame sizes Depend on build (20/40/48 panels) Default 20 panels Derive from GET_FIRMWARE_VERSION rows × cols. Pixel row order inside a panel block Controller passes blocks through. Panel firmware (reference/panel/): first 20 pixels = top row. But the controller's own error glyph (ErrorGlyph.cpp:72-82) packs the bottom row first, citing the g6_04 spec ("origin bottom-left, pixel_num = row_from_bottom × 20 + col"). pat-encoder.js/pat-parser.js: top row first. g6-encoding.js ("matches MATLAB g6_encode_panel.m"): bottom row first. Top row first, as the panel firmware does (matches pat-encoder.js). Confirmed on hardware: the controller's "CE NN" glyph appears vertically flipped (upside-down digits above "CE"). This is a controller-firmware bug in ErrorGlyph.cpp, and the g6_04 spec text and g6-encoding.js are out of step with the panel firmware. Partial arenas (panel mask with gaps) Mask popcount checked only Encoder assumes full grid Full grid only for now.

docs.title: Host-side decisions
docs.text:
Behaviour the library adds on top of the wire protocol, as agreed in review.

  • Close sends ALL_OFF by default. Closing the connection (explicitly or by leaving a with block, including on an exception) sends ALL_OFF before releasing the port, so the arena goes dark. This can be turned off per connection with Device.open(..., all_off_on_close=False) (or the all_off_on_close attribute), for example to leave a stimulus running after a script exits. The ALL_OFF is best-effort: if the device has already disappeared, close still releases the port and does not raise.
  • Patterns are built from pixel arrays. The library builds and parses .pat files and stream-frame payloads from whole-arena pixel arrays (GS2: 0/1, GS16: 0–15), handling panel splitting, row order within panels, packing, parity and CRCs. numpy is a required dependency (decided 2026-11-06; it was an optional extra before): images may be numpy arrays or nested lists, and frames are returned as uint8 numpy arrays.
  • Pixel array orientation is selectable, top-origin by default. Every function that takes or returns a pixel array has an origin argument named after matplotlib's imshow: "upper" (default) means row 0 is the top of the arena; "lower" means row 0 is the bottom (the pat-encoder.js / MATLAB / G4 convention). Columns run left to right in both. The library converts to the on-wire order (top row first within each panel) internally.
  • Auto-detect is optional, and probes by default. VID/PID 16C0:0483 matches any Teensy running USB serial, so:
    • An explicit port skips detection entirely; no other port is touched.
    • find_ports() lists VID/PID matches and sends nothing.
    • With no port given, a single match is opened directly. With several matches, each is confirmed with GET_CONTROLLER_INFO (01 C2); this probing is on by default and can be turned off with probe=False. If the choice is still ambiguous, an error lists the candidates and asks for an explicit port.
  • Unsupported commands are refused locally. On connect the library reads GET_CONTROLLER_INFO (0xC2) and, when capability bit 7 is set, GET_FIRMWARE_VERSION (0xCB). A method whose command is gated by a capability bit or firmware flag that the device does not advertise (see Capability and feature flags) raises UnsupportedCommand without sending anything, so it can never trigger the CE 01 glyph. Ungated commands are always sent. Opcodes this firmware does not implement at all (the reserved ones and the newer-firmware commands listed under Discrepancies) are not exposed.

  • Diagnostic and bench commands live in a diagnostics namespace. All firmware commands are supported, but the ones meant for bench work and post-mortems are grouped under device.diagnostics so the main API stays focused on running experiments: GET_HEALTH (0xCA), GET_CRASHREPORT (0xCC), GET_SD_INFO / SET_SD_DIAG (0xCD / 0xCE), GET/SET_DIAG_OUTPUT (0xC3 / 0xC4) and GET/SET_SPI_CLOCK (0xC5 / 0xC6). The telemetry ring (0xA8 / 0xA9) has its own device.telemetry group (changed in M6: frame and state events are useful for ordinary experiment logs, not just debugging). The telemetry watchdog bits (SET_TELEMETRY bits 4–6: disable or starve the watchdog, which resets the controller) are not exposed; the library always sends them as 0. Panel firmware update (0xE0, 0xE3, 0xC8, 0xC9) is maintenance rather than bench debugging and gets its own group, device.panel_firmware.

  • Arenas are described by geometry, with built-in presets. An Arena has a full panel grid (rows × cols), the installed columns, and optionally a name and an arena id (written to the .pat header arena_id field; the controller ignores it). The eight G6 arenas from the JS registry are built in as presets: 1 G6_2x10, 2 G6_2x8of10, 3 G6_3x12of18, 4 G6_3x16_full, 5 G6_3x10, 6 G6_4x10, 7 G6_1x12of18, 8 G6_3x10of14. A maDisplayTools YAML arena registry can be loaded optionally to add or override presets; this needs PyYAML, provided as an optional extra (arena-interface[yaml]).

  • Patterns are full-grid. The panel mask is always "all panels"; columns that are not installed are left blank. This matches the JS tools (pattern-set.js: the controller cannot play partial-arena patterns).
  • Rig geometry is mapped onto the firmware build. The rig (physical arena) may be smaller than the grid the controller firmware is built for (e.g. a 3×10 rig on 4×10 firmware; panels that are not present are ignored). Stream frames and patterns encoded for upload use the firmware's grid, following studio-stream-geometry.js: grid column c → firmware column c (installed columns must fit); rig rows are repeated up the frame to fill the firmware's rows. Firmware that does not report its geometry (no capability bit 7) can only stream 20-panel arenas unless the user states the geometry. Row repetition vs. blank padding is not yet verified on hardware.
  • Streaming means polling, exposed as blocking iterators. The firmware sends nothing unsolicited, so:
    • device.telemetry.events() drains the telemetry ring continuously and yields frame, state and command events. A record is acknowledged only after it has been yielded (by the next poll), and the library remembers the last sequence number, so stopping and restarting the loop neither loses nor repeats events. Sequence gaps (ring overflow) are logged and counted.
    • device.sample(read, rate_hz=...) calls any read method at a fixed rate (drift-free schedule; late samples are skipped and counted).
    • Timestamps are wall-clock (time.time()). Telemetry times are derived from the controller's microsecond clock relative to the t_now_us in each reply, so the 71.6-minute wrap needs no unwrapping. Records written before the controller's last reset (the ring survives resets) have no host time. The raw controller time is always kept.
    • Host-paced frame playback (M6b, scope agreed 2026-11-05): both pre-computed sequences and live (closed-loop) frame choice; both SD frame positions (SET_FRAME_POSITION) and streamed images (STREAM_FRAME); late frames are either skipped (keep the schedule) or all sent, chosen by the caller; feedback on missed timing is always available; blocking and background (thread) playback. No FicTrac bridge for now. Implemented as dev.play_frames() / dev.play_images() (blocking), dev.start_frames() / dev.start_images() (background, returning a Playback), and dev.pace() (live), with late="skip"|"send", an optional refresh_rate=, a PlaybackReport and verify=True for SD frames; configuration problems raise a PerformanceWarning. Measured on a 2x10 controller: about 575 frame positions/s (SD-limited) and 1000-2600 streamed frames/s, but only one frame per panel refresh (300 Hz there) is displayed.

docs.title: device
docs.text:
High-level interface to a G6 arena controller.

from arena_interface import Device, TrialMode

with Device.open() as dev:                # auto-detect
    print(dev.firmware_version)
    dev.start_trial(1, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=60, duration=5)

Thread safety: a Device may be shared between threads. Each method is atomic (the wire protocol allows only one request at a time and the device serialises them), and multi-step methods such as PatternLibrary.upload hold a lock for their whole sequence. Sequences of calls made by your own code are not atomic; use your own lock if another thread must not interleave.

docs.title: pattern
docs.text:
Patterns from pixel arrays: build and read .pat files and stream frames.

A Pattern holds one image per frame for a whole arena: rows * 20 pixels high and cols * 20 wide, with values 0/1 (GS2) or 0-15 (GS16). Images may be numpy arrays or nested lists; frames come back as numpy arrays.

import numpy as np
from arena_interface import Arena, GrayLevel, Pattern

h, w = Arena.preset("G6_2x10").pixel_shape
x = np.arange(w)
stripes = [np.tile(np.where((x + f) % 20 < 10, 15, 0), (h, 1)) for f in range(20)]
pattern = Pattern.from_frames(stripes, gray_level=GrayLevel.GS16)
data = pattern.to_bytes()               # a .pat file

Orientation: by default row 0 of an image is the top of the arena (origin="upper", as in numpy and matplotlib's imshow). Pass origin="lower" for row 0 at the bottom, the convention of the MATLAB and JavaScript tools. Columns run left to right either way.

The library converts to the on-wire layout: panels in row-major order from the bottom row of panels, and within each panel block the first 20 pixels are the panel's top row (as the panel firmware reads them; see docs/PROTOCOL.md).

docs.title: playback
docs.text:
Host-paced playback: the computer decides when each frame is shown.

Three ways to use it, all on a Device:

dev.show_pattern(4)
report = dev.play_frames(range(200), fps=200)        # frames of an SD pattern
report = dev.play_images(images, fps=120)            # streamed images

player = dev.start_frames(range(200), fps=200)       # same, in the background
report = player.wait()

for tick in dev.pace(rate_hz=200, duration=10):      # live: you choose each frame
    dev.show_frame(choose_frame())

Timing: frames are scheduled against a fixed clock (no drift). The scheduler sleeps until just before each slot and then busy-waits for sub-millisecond accuracy. When a frame cannot be sent on time, late="skip" drops frames whose slot has passed so the sequence keeps its schedule, and late="send" sends every frame, so the sequence runs long. Either way the PlaybackReport says what happened, and falling behind is logged on arena_interface.playback.

A frame is only displayed if it stays in place for at least one refresh of the controller, so fps should not exceed the refresh rate (dev.refresh_rate); a PerformanceWarning is issued if it does. Frames of an SD pattern also wait for the controller's SD read, which occasionally stalls, so at fps close to the refresh rate a frame can now and then be replaced unseen; play_frames(..., verify=True) reports it.

docs.title: streaming
docs.text:
Continuous data from the controller: telemetry events and periodic samples.

The controller never sends data on its own, so both are polling loops exposed as blocking iterators:

with Device.open() as dev:
    for event in dev.telemetry.events(duration=10):
        print(event.time, event.record)

    for s in dev.sample(dev.io.read_analog_in, rate_hz=100, duration=5):
        print(s.time, s.value.ain1_mv)

Times are wall-clock seconds (time.time()).

Request builders and response decoders for every controller command.

Each command has a builder that validates its arguments and returns a Request: the bytes to send, the opcode the reply will echo, a suitable timeout, the kind of exchange, and the capability or firmware flag the device must advertise. Replies are turned into dataclasses by the decode_* functions.

Exceptions raised by arena_interface.

Every exception the library raises on purpose derives from DeviceError, so a caller can catch them all with one except clause:

docs.title: testing
docs.text:
A simulated G6 arena controller for tests, examples and development.

FakePort behaves like a pyserial port connected to a controller. Behind it, a FakeController parses the bytes written to the port the way the firmware does and answers with the same replies: status codes, messages, payload layouts and side effects (error glyphs that stop the display, commands refused while the display runs, index shifts after deleting a pattern, and so on). It keeps an in-memory SD card, the telemetry ring and the I/O state.

from arena_interface.testing import FakePort
from arena_interface.transport import Transport

with Transport(FakePort()) as link:
    ...

The controller can also inject faults: unplugging the device, going silent, delaying replies, or emitting debug text. A controller outlives its ports, so a test can unplug, then connect a new FakePort(controller) to simulate a reconnect.

What is not emulated: panel pixels (frames are accepted, not rendered), the precise wording of panel-programming messages, and refresh timing beyond a simple frames-sent estimate.

"""List serial ports, then connect to one by name.

Shows: find_ports() (Teensy candidates and all ports), Device.open(port),
probe=False.
Requires: a connected controller (or use --simulate).
"""

import argparse

from arena_interface import Device, DeviceNotFound, find_ports


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    ports = find_ports(all_ports=True)
    print("USB serial ports:")
    for port in (p for p in ports if p.vid is not None):
        print(f"  {port.device:15} {port.vid:04X}:{port.pid:04X}  {port.description}")
    print(f"({sum(p.vid is None for p in ports)} non-USB ports not shown)")

    candidates = find_ports()  # Teensy USB ids only; nothing is sent to them
    print(f"Teensy candidates: {[p.device for p in candidates] or 'none'}")

    if args.simulate:
        dev = Device.open(simulate=True)
    elif args.port:
        dev = Device.open(args.port)  # an explicit port skips detection
    else:
        try:
            # Without probing, more than one candidate is an error.
            dev = Device.open(probe=False)
        except DeviceNotFound as exc:
            print(f"Could not choose a port: {exc}")
            return

    with dev:
        print(f"Connected on {dev.port_name}: {dev.firmware_version}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Context manager versus manual open/close, and leaving the display on.

"""Context manager versus manual open/close, and leaving the display on.

Shows: `with Device.open(...)`, try/finally with close(), is_open, and
all_off_on_close=False to keep a stimulus running after the script ends.
Requires: a connected controller (or use --simulate).
"""

import argparse

from arena_interface import Device


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    # 1. Context manager: the arena is blanked (ALL_OFF) and the port released
    #    when the block ends, even if an exception is raised inside it.
    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        dev.all_on()
        print(f"inside the block: open={dev.is_open}")
    print(f"after the block:  open={dev.is_open}")

    # 2. Manual: the same, written out.
    dev = Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate)
    try:
        dev.all_on()
    finally:
        dev.close()  # safe to call twice, and after the device has gone

    # 3. Leave the arena lit when the script exits.
    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate, all_off_on_close=False) as dev:
        dev.all_on()
    print("arena left on; run ALL_OFF (e.g. example 05) to blank it")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text:
Run trials from a pattern stored on the SD card.

"""Run trials from a pattern stored on the SD card.

Shows: start_trial() in open loop (forwards and backwards), closed loop and
with a controller-timed duration; polling frame_position.
Requires: a controller with at least one pattern on its SD card (or
--simulate, which provides demo patterns).
"""

import argparse
import time

from arena_interface import Device, TrialMode


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--pattern", type=int, default=1, help="pattern id (1-based)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        print(f"Pattern {args.pattern}: {dev.patterns.name(args.pattern)}")

        # Open loop: the controller advances frames by itself.
        dev.start_trial(args.pattern, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=30)
        for _ in range(3):
            time.sleep(0.2)
            print(f"  forwards  {dev.frame_position}")

        dev.start_trial(args.pattern, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=-30)
        time.sleep(0.2)
        print(f"  backwards {dev.frame_position}")

        # Closed loop: frame rate = Analog In 1 voltage x gain / 10.
        dev.start_trial(args.pattern, TrialMode.CLOSED_LOOP, gain=20)
        print("  closed loop running (drive Analog In 1 to move the pattern)")
        time.sleep(0.2)

        # A duration makes the controller stop the trial on its own.
        dev.start_trial(args.pattern, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=60, duration=0.5)
        time.sleep(0.7)
        print("  timed trial finished; the arena is dark again")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Manage the patterns on the controller's SD card.

Shows: iterating device.patterns, info(), upload(), download(), rename(),
delete() and archive(). The example uploads its own pattern and removes it
again, so the card ends as it started.
Requires: a controller with an SD card (or --simulate). The display is
stopped first, because transfers need it off.
"""

import argparse

from arena_interface import Device, Pattern


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        dev.stop()
        for entry in dev.patterns:
            info = dev.patterns.info(entry.pattern_id)
            print(
                f"{entry.pattern_id:3} {entry.name:30} {info.frame_count:5} frames "
                f"{info.gray_level.name} {info.rows}x{info.cols}"
            )

        # A one-frame pattern sized for this controller.
        height, width = dev.arena.pixel_shape
        frame = [
            [15 if x < width // 2 else 0 for x in range(width)] for _ in range(height)
        ]
        pid = dev.patterns.upload("zz_example_08.pat", Pattern.from_frames([frame]))
        print(f"Uploaded as id {pid}")

        data = dev.patterns.download(pid)
        print(f"Downloaded {len(data)} bytes; frames: {len(Pattern.from_bytes(data))}")

        pid = dev.patterns.rename(pid, "zz_example_08_renamed.pat")
        print(f"Renamed; id is now {pid}: {dev.patterns.name(pid)}")

        dev.patterns.delete(pid)
        print(f"Deleted; {len(dev.patterns)} patterns remain")

        if args.simulate:  # a full card can take a while to download
            print(f"SD archive: {len(dev.patterns.archive())} bytes (ZIP)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text:
Build a pattern from pixel arrays and save it as a .pat file.

"""Build a pattern from pixel arrays and save it as a .pat file.

Shows: Pattern.from_frames() with numpy arrays (nested lists work too), an
arena preset, gray levels, duty cycle, origin="lower" for bottom-origin data,
to_bytes() and reading the file back with Pattern.from_bytes(). Upload the
result with device.patterns.upload("grating.pat", pattern).
Requires: nothing (no controller needed). Writes grating.pat.
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from arena_interface import Arena, GrayLevel, Pattern


def grating(height: int, width: int, shift: int, period: int = 20) -> np.ndarray:
    """A triangle-wave grating with 16 brightness levels, moved by `shift` pixels."""
    phase = ((np.arange(width) + shift) % period) / period
    row = np.round(15 * (1 - np.abs(2 * phase - 1))).astype(np.uint8)
    return np.tile(row, (height, 1))


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (unused: no device needed)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--simulate", action="store_true", help="accepted for consistency"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--arena", default="G6_2x10", help="arena preset name")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("grating.pat"))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    arena = Arena.preset(args.arena)
    height, width = arena.pixel_shape
    frames = [grating(height, width, shift) for shift in range(20)]

    pattern = Pattern.from_frames(
        frames, gray_level=GrayLevel.GS16, arena=arena, duty_cycle=128
    )
    args.output.write_bytes(pattern.to_bytes())
    print(f"Wrote {args.output}: {pattern}")

    # Orientation: by default row 0 is the TOP of the arena. Data whose row 0 is
    # the bottom (MATLAB / JS convention) needs origin="lower".
    marker = np.zeros((height, width), dtype=np.uint8)
    marker[0, 0] = 15
    top = Pattern.from_frames([marker], arena=arena)
    bottom = Pattern.from_frames([marker], arena=arena, origin="lower")
    row_top = int(np.argmax(top.frame(0)[:, 0]))  # frame() returns a numpy array
    row_bottom = int(np.argmax(bottom.frame(0)[:, 0]))
    print(f"marker in row {row_top} vs {row_bottom} (rows counted from the top)")

    again = Pattern.from_bytes(args.output.read_bytes())
    print(f"Read back: {again}; identical: {again == pattern}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: 10_stream_images.py
docs.text:
Send images from the host straight to the arena.

"""Send images from the host straight to the arena.

Shows: stream_image() with a moving bar in a simple timed loop. Streamed
frames need no SD card. (Precisely paced playback is a planned feature; this
loop just sleeps between frames.)
Requires: a connected controller (or use --simulate).
"""

import argparse
import time

from arena_interface import Device, GrayLevel


def bar(height: int, width: int, x0: int, bar_width: int = 20) -> list[list[int]]:
    """An image with a vertical bright bar starting at column x0."""
    row = [1 if (x - x0) % width < bar_width else 0 for x in range(width)]
    return [list(row) for _ in range(height)]


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--fps", type=float, default=30.0, help="frames per second")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=2.0, help="how long to run")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        height, width = dev.arena.pixel_shape
        frames = int(args.fps * args.seconds)
        start = time.monotonic()
        for n in range(frames):
            dev.stream_image(bar(height, width, x0=n * 4), gray_level=GrayLevel.GS2)
            time.sleep(max(0.0, start + (n + 1) / args.fps - time.monotonic()))
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        print(
            f"Streamed {frames} frames in {elapsed:.2f} s ({frames / elapsed:.1f} fps)"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Analog output and inputs.

Shows: io.analog_out (set, and read back from the DAC), a lookup table that
follows the displayed frame, the frame-number output mode, and
io.read_analog_in().
Requires: a controller with the extended I/O capability and a pattern on
its SD card (or --simulate). Use a pattern with several frames to see the
table step. The analog output BNC changes voltage while this runs.
"""

import argparse

from arena_interface import AoLutMode, AoMode, Device, TrialMode


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--pattern", type=int, default=1, help="pattern id (1-based)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        io = dev.io
        io.set_analog_out_mode(AoMode.PROGRAMMABLE)
        io.analog_out = 2500
        print(f"Analog out set to 2500 mV, DAC reads back {io.analog_out} mV")

        # Lookup table: one level per frame index (up to 21 levels).
        io.load_analog_table([0, 1250, 2500, 3750, 5000], AoLutMode.FRAME_LOCKED)
        dev.show_pattern(args.pattern)
        for frame in range(min(5, dev.frame_position.frame_count)):
            dev.show_frame(frame)
            print(f"  frame {frame}: analog out {io.analog_out} mV")

        # Frame-number mode: 0 V at the first frame, 5 V at the last.
        io.set_analog_out_mode(AoMode.FRAME_NUMBER)
        dev.start_trial(args.pattern, TrialMode.SHOW_FRAME)
        dev.show_frame(dev.frame_position.frame_count - 1)
        print(f"Frame-number mode, last frame: {io.analog_out} mV")
        io.set_analog_out_mode(AoMode.PROGRAMMABLE)

        inputs = io.read_analog_in()
        print(f"Analog in: {inputs.ain1_mv} mV, {inputs.ain2_mv} mV")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        io = dev.io
        for number, port in enumerate(io.dio_roles(), start=1):
            level = "high" if port.high else "low"
            print(f"Port {number}: {port.role.name:20} level={level}")

        io.set_dio_role(1, DioRole.OUT_PROGRAMMABLE)
        io.set_digital_out(1, True)
        print(f"Port 1 driven high; levels now {io.read_digital()}")
        io.set_digital_out(1, False)

        roles = io.dio_roles()

            try:
                io.set_digital_out(2, True)
            except CommandError as exc:
                print(f"Refused as expected: {exc.message}")

"""Log what the arena actually displayed, from the controller's own record.

Shows: telemetry.events() during an open-loop trial, FrameRecord and
StateRecord events with wall-clock times, and writing a frame log to CSV.
The controller timestamps each frame change itself, so the log is more
accurate than timing on the host.
Requires: a controller with telemetry and a pattern on its SD card (or
--simulate). Writes frame_log.csv.
"""

import argparse
import csv
from pathlib import Path

from arena_interface import Device, FrameRecord, StateRecord, TrialMode


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=1.0, help="trial length")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("frame_log.csv"))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        dev.telemetry.drain()  # discard anything logged before now
        dev.start_trial(1, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=20, duration=args.seconds)

        frames = 0
        with args.output.open("w", newline="") as f:
            writer = csv.writer(f)
            writer.writerow(["time_s", "pattern", "frame"])
            stream = dev.telemetry.events(duration=args.seconds + 0.3)
            for event in stream:
                rec = event.record
                if isinstance(rec, FrameRecord):
                    writer.writerow([f"{event.time:.6f}", rec.pattern_id, rec.index])
                    frames += 1
                elif isinstance(rec, StateRecord) and rec.new_state is not None:
                    print(f"{event.time:.3f}  state -> {rec.new_state.name}")
    print(f"Logged {frames} frame changes to {args.output} (lost: {stream.lost})")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Arena presets, partial arenas, and rigs smaller than the firmware's grid.

Shows: the built-in Arena presets, installed columns, drawing on a rig's full
grid, Pattern.fit_to() onto a controller's panel grid (e.g. a 3x10 rig on
4x10 firmware), and stream_image() with arena=, which fits automatically.
Requires: a connected controller (or use --simulate).
"""

import argparse

from arena_interface import PRESETS, Arena, Device, GrayLevel, Pattern


def columns_lit(rig: Arena) -> list[list[int]]:
    """Light every installed column; uninstalled grid columns stay blank."""
    height, width = rig.pixel_shape
    return [
        [1 if x // 20 in rig.columns else 0 for x in range(width)]
        for _ in range(height)
    ]


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--rig", default="G6_2x8of10", help="arena preset of the rig")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    for name, arena in PRESETS.items():
        print(
            f"{name:14} id {arena.arena_id}  {arena.rows}x{arena.cols} grid, "
            f"columns {arena.columns[0]}-{arena.columns[-1]}"
        )

    # Offline: a 3x10 rig drawn at its own size, placed on a 4x10 firmware grid.
    small = Arena.preset("G6_3x10")
    pattern = Pattern.from_frames(
        [columns_lit(small)], gray_level=GrayLevel.GS2, arena=small
    )
    fitted = pattern.fit_to(4, 10)
    print(f"{pattern} -> fitted for 4x10 firmware: {fitted}")

    # On the device: stream an image drawn for the rig; it is fitted to the
    # controller's grid (an error explains it if the rig cannot fit).
    rig = Arena.preset(args.rig)
    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        installed = len(rig.columns)
        print(f"Controller grid: {dev.arena_shape}; rig: {rig} ({installed} columns)")
        dev.stream_image(columns_lit(rig), gray_level=GrayLevel.GS2, arena=rig)
        print("Streamed the rig image")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Update the panels' own firmware through the controller.

"""Update the panels' own firmware through the controller.

Shows: panel_firmware.info(), upload() (with CRC check), verify() and
program(). Programming is only done when you ask for it with --program.
Requires: a controller with an SD card and a panel image file (--image), or
--simulate, which uses a dummy image. The display is stopped first.
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

from arena_interface import Device


def dummy_image() -> bytes:
    """A stand-in image with the 32-byte footer the controller reads."""
    return bytes(8192) + b"G6PANEL\0" + b"sim-1.0".ljust(16, b"\0") + bytes(8)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--image", type=Path, help="panel firmware image to upload")
    parser.add_argument("--program", type=int, metavar="PANEL", help="flash this panel")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        dev.stop()
        fw = dev.panel_firmware
        print(f"Stored image: {fw.info() or 'none'}")

        image = (
            args.image.read_bytes()
            if args.image
            else (dummy_image() if args.simulate else None)
        )
        if image is None:
            print("Pass --image FILE to upload a panel image.")
            return
        crc = fw.upload(image)
        print(f"Uploaded {len(image)} bytes, CRC-32 0x{crc:08x}: {fw.info()}")

        panel = args.program or (1 if args.simulate else None)
        if panel is None:
            print("Pass --program N to flash panel N (1-based).")
            return
        print(f"Before: {fw.verify(panel)}")
        print(f"Programming panel {panel}: {fw.program(panel)}")
        print(f"After:  {fw.verify(panel)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Handling errors: what each exception means and how to recover.

"""Handling errors: what each exception means and how to recover.

Shows: CommandError (the controller refused), ValueError (rejected locally
before sending), UnsupportedCommand (older firmware), DeviceTimeout (no
answer), and DeviceError as the catch-all base class.
Requires: a connected controller (or --simulate, which can also fake a
silent device; on hardware the timeout case is skipped).
"""

import argparse

from arena_interface import (
    CommandError,
    Device,
    DeviceError,
    DeviceTimeout,
    ErrorCode,
    UnsupportedCommand,
)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        dev.all_on()
        try:
            dev.patterns.download(1)  # transfers need the display off
        except CommandError as exc:  # exc.status says why: here DISPLAY_ACTIVE
            print(f"CommandError ({ErrorCode(exc.status).name}): {exc.message}")
        dev.stop()

        try:
            dev.refresh_rate = 0  # out of range
        except ValueError as exc:
            print(f"ValueError, nothing sent: {exc}")

        try:
            block = dev.telemetry.read_block()
            print(f"Telemetry available ({len(block.records)} records waiting)")
        except UnsupportedCommand as exc:
            print(f"UnsupportedCommand, nothing sent: {exc}")

        if dev.simulator is not None:
            dev.simulator.muted = True  # the fake device stops answering
            try:
                dev.all_off()
            except DeviceTimeout as exc:
                print(f"DeviceTimeout: {exc}")
            dev.simulator.muted = False

        try:
            dev.start_trial(999)  # no such pattern
        except DeviceError as exc:  # base class of every library error
            print(f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Recover from a controller reset or an unplugged cable.

Shows: reset() (reboots the controller and closes the connection),
reconnect() (waits for the same controller to come back, checked by its MAC
address), and catching DeviceDisconnected to reconnect after an unplug.
Requires: a connected controller (or --simulate, which fakes the unplug).
On hardware, unplug and replug the USB cable when asked.
"""

import argparse

from arena_interface import Device, DeviceDisconnected


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        print(f"Connected to {dev.info.mac} on {dev.port_name}")

        dev.reset()
        print(f"Reset sent; connection open: {dev.is_open}")
        dev.reconnect(timeout=15)
        print(f"Back after reset; uptime {dev.diagnostics.health().uptime_ms} ms")

        if dev.simulator is not None:
            dev.simulator.unplug()
        else:
            input("Unplug the USB cable, then press Enter... ")
        try:
            dev.all_off()
        except DeviceDisconnected as exc:
            print(f"Lost the device: {exc}")
            if dev.simulator is None:
                print("Plug the cable back in (waiting up to 30 s)")
            dev.reconnect(timeout=30)
            dev.all_off()
            print("Reconnected and working again")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Share one Device between threads.

"""Share one Device between threads.

Shows: a background thread sampling the analog inputs while the main thread
runs trials. Every Device method is atomic, so the two never corrupt each
other's exchanges; a thread just waits briefly while the other's request is
on the wire.
Requires: a controller with a pattern on its SD card and the extended I/O
capability (or --simulate).
"""

import argparse
import threading
import time

from arena_interface import Device, TrialMode


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        readings = []
        stop = threading.Event()

        def sampler() -> None:
            for s in dev.sample(dev.io.read_analog_in, rate_hz=50):
                readings.append(s)
                if stop.is_set():
                    return

        thread = threading.Thread(target=sampler)
        thread.start()
        for rate in (10, 20, 40):
            dev.start_trial(1, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=rate)
            time.sleep(0.3)
            print(f"rate {rate:2} fps: frame {dev.frame_position.index}")
        dev.stop()
        stop.set()
        thread.join()
        print(f"Background thread took {len(readings)} samples meanwhile")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.text:
A complete experiment run: upload a stimulus, run timed trials, save logs.

"""A complete experiment run: upload a stimulus, run timed trials, save logs.

Shows: a multi-step workflow combining Pattern, patterns.upload(overwrite=True),
start_trial() with a controller-timed duration, and telemetry.events() to
save, per trial, the frames the arena actually showed.
Requires: a controller with an SD card and telemetry (or --simulate).
Writes one CSV per trial into experiment_logs/.
"""

import argparse
import csv
from pathlib import Path

from arena_interface import Arena, Device, FrameRecord, Pattern, TrialMode

TRIALS = [("slow", 10), ("fast", 40), ("reverse", -20)]  # (name, frames per second)


def make_stimulus(arena: Arena) -> Pattern:
    """A 20-frame moving bar sized for the controller's grid."""
    h, w = arena.pixel_shape
    frames = [
        [[15 if (x - f * 10) % w < 20 else 0 for x in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]
        for f in range(20)
    ]
    return Pattern.from_frames(frames, arena=arena)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=1.0, help="trial length")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("experiment_logs"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    args.output.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        dev.stop()
        pid = dev.patterns.upload(
            "moving_bar.pat", make_stimulus(dev.arena), overwrite=True
        )
        dev.telemetry.drain()  # start the logs from here

        for name, rate in TRIALS:
            dev.start_trial(
                pid, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=rate, duration=args.seconds
            )
            path = args.output / f"trial_{name}.csv"
            with path.open("w", newline="") as f:
                writer = csv.writer(f)
                writer.writerow(["time_s", "frame"])
                for event in dev.telemetry.events(duration=args.seconds + 0.2):
                    if isinstance(event.record, FrameRecord):
                        writer.writerow([f"{event.time:.6f}", event.record.index])
            print(f"trial {name:8} ({rate:+} fps) -> {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: 23_ao_calibration.py
docs.text:
Calibrate Analog In 1 against the analog output with a loopback cable.

"""Calibrate Analog In 1 against the analog output with a loopback cable.

Shows: a measurement workflow: step io.analog_out, read io.read_analog_in()
several times at each level, fit gain and offset by least squares, and save
the table. Analog inputs are uncalibrated in firmware, so a fit like this
converts their readings to real millivolts.
Requires: a BNC cable from the analog output to Analog In 1 (or --simulate,
which fakes the cable with a small gain and offset error).
Writes ao_calibration.csv.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import statistics
from pathlib import Path

from arena_interface import AoMode, Device


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--steps", type=int, default=11, help="levels from 0 to 5000 mV"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=Path("ao_calibration.csv"))
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        if dev.simulator is not None:
            dev.simulator.analog_loopback = (1.013, -27.0)  # gain, offset (mV)
        dev.io.set_analog_out_mode(AoMode.PROGRAMMABLE)
        table = []
        for i in range(args.steps):
            dev.io.analog_out = round(5000 * i / (args.steps - 1))
            out_mv = dev.io.analog_out  # what the DAC actually produces
            readings = [
                s.value.ain1_mv for s in dev.sample(dev.io.read_analog_in, 200, count=5)
            ]
            table.append((out_mv, statistics.mean(readings)))
        dev.io.analog_out = 0

    xs, ys = zip(*table, strict=True)
    gain, offset = statistics.linear_regression(xs, ys)  # ain1 = gain * out + offset
    residual = max(abs(y - (gain * x + offset)) for x, y in table)
    with args.output.open("w", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.writer(f)
        writer.writerow(["ao_mv", "ain1_mean_mv"])
        writer.writerows(table)
    print(f"Analog In 1 = {gain:.4f} x output {offset:+.1f} mV")
    print(f"Largest residual: {residual:.1f} mV")
    print(f"To correct a reading: true_mv = (ain1_mv {-offset:+.1f}) / {gain:.4f}")
    print(f"Table saved to {args.output}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: 24_host_playback.py
docs.text:
Play frame sequences at a fixed rate, paced by the computer.

"""Play frame sequences at a fixed rate, paced by the computer.

Shows: play_frames() (frames of an SD pattern, with verify=True to check what
the controller displayed), play_images() (streamed images), and
start_frames() running in the background while the script does other work.
Requires: a controller with a pattern of 20+ frames on its SD card (or
--simulate).
"""

import argparse
import time

from arena_interface import Device, GrayLevel


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--pattern", type=int, default=1, help="pattern id (1-based)")
    parser.add_argument("--fps", type=float, default=100.0, help="frames per second")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        # 1. Frames of an SD pattern: forwards, then backwards.
        dev.show_pattern(args.pattern)
        n = dev.frame_position.frame_count
        frames = [*range(n), *reversed(range(n))]
        report = dev.play_frames(frames, fps=args.fps, late="skip", verify=True)
        print(f"SD frames:  {report}")

        # 2. Streamed images: a bar moving across the arena.
        h, w = dev.arena.pixel_shape
        images = [
            [[1 if (x - 8 * f) % w < 20 else 0 for x in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]
            for f in range(w // 8)
        ]
        report = dev.play_images(images, fps=args.fps, gray_level=GrayLevel.GS2)
        print(f"Streamed:   {report}")

        # 3. In the background: the script keeps working meanwhile.
        with dev.start_frames(frames, fps=args.fps) as player:
            while player.running:
                print(f"  background progress {player.progress}/{player.total}")
                time.sleep(0.2)
        print(f"Background: {player.report}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Analog In 1 and moves the pattern by a step proportional to the voltage,
then shows that frame. tick.skipped says when the loop fell behind, and
pacer.report summarises the timing.
Requires: a controller with a pattern on its SD card and the extended I/O
capability (or --simulate, which drives Analog In 1 with a slow sine wave).
"""

import argparse
import math

from arena_interface import Device


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--pattern", type=int, default=1, help="pattern id (1-based)")
    parser.add_argument("--rate", type=float, default=100.0, help="frames per second")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=2.0, help="how long to run")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--gain", type=float, default=2.0, help="frames per tick per volt"
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        dev.show_pattern(args.pattern)
        frames = dev.frame_position.frame_count
        position = 0.0
        pacer = dev.pace(args.rate, duration=args.seconds, late="skip")
        for tick in pacer:
            if dev.simulator is not None:  # pretend something drives the input
                dev.simulator.analog_in = (round(3000 * math.sin(tick.index / 40)), 0)
            volts = dev.io.read_analog_in().ain1_mv / 1000
            position += args.gain * volts * (1 + tick.skipped)  # catch up after skips
            dev.show_frame(int(position) % frames)
        print(pacer.report)
        print(f"final frame {dev.frame_position.index} of {frames}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Live plot of the analog inputs with matplotlib.

Shows: device.sample() feeding a matplotlib line plot that updates as data
arrives. With a non-interactive backend (e.g. MPLBACKEND=Agg) the final plot
is only saved to analog_plot.png.
The live window uses matplotlib's default Tk backend (TkAgg), which needs
Python's tkinter; on Linux install it with your distribution's package if
missing (e.g. ``sudo apt install python3-tk``).
Requires: matplotlib (``pip install matplotlib``) and a controller with the
extended I/O capability, or --simulate, which drives a sine wave through a
simulated cable from the analog output to Analog In 1.
"""

import argparse
import math
from collections import deque

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from arena_interface import Device

NON_INTERACTIVE = {"agg", "pdf", "ps", "svg", "cairo", "template"}


def redraw(ax, line1, line2, t, a1, a2) -> None:
    """Show the latest data and scroll the time axis."""
    line1.set_data(t, a1)
    line2.set_data(t, a2)
    ax.set_xlim(t[0], max(t[-1], t[0] + 1))


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, default=10.0, help="how long to plot")
    parser.add_argument("--rate", type=float, default=50.0, help="samples per second")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    live = plt.get_backend().lower() not in NON_INTERACTIVE
    fig, ax = plt.subplots()
    (line1,) = ax.plot([], [], label="Analog In 1")
    (line2,) = ax.plot([], [], label="Analog In 2")
    ax.set(xlabel="time (s)", ylabel="mV", ylim=(-10500, 10500))
    ax.legend(loc="upper right")
    t, a1, a2 = (deque(maxlen=int(args.rate * 10)) for _ in range(3))

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        if dev.simulator is not None:
            dev.simulator.analog_loopback = (1.0, 0.0)
        start = None
        for s in dev.sample(dev.io.read_analog_in, args.rate, duration=args.seconds):
            start = start or s.time
            t.append(s.time - start)
            a1.append(s.value.ain1_mv)
            a2.append(s.value.ain2_mv)
            if dev.simulator is not None:
                dev.io.analog_out = round(2500 + 2400 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * t[-1]))
            if live and len(t) % 5 == 0:
                redraw(ax, line1, line2, t, a1, a2)
                plt.pause(0.001)
    redraw(ax, line1, line2, t, a1, a2)
    fig.savefig("analog_plot.png")
    print("Saved analog_plot.png")
    if live:
        plt.show()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
