Stream a webcam to the arena in real time. A box with the arena's aspect ratio, moved and resized with the mouse, picks the part of the picture that is shrunk to the arena's pixels and streamed. GS16 with contrast stretching by default; --gs2 uses dithered on/off pixels. --rotate DEG (0-360) moves the picture's centre around the arena. Needs OpenCV (uv sync --extra camera); --simulate uses a moving test picture.

"""Stream a webcam to the arena in real time, through a box you move.

Shows: capturing with OpenCV, cropping a region with the arena's aspect
ratio (chosen live with the mouse), shrinking it to dev.arena.pixel_shape and
sending it with dev.stream_image() as fast as the camera delivers frames.
GS16 with contrast stretching by default; --gs2 sends on/off pixels with
ordered dithering. The image is mirrored, like a mirror you face; --no-mirror
turns that off. See roi_view.py for the mouse and keyboard controls.
The camera is asked for compressed MJPG frames at 30 fps: raw (YUYV) frames
need several times the USB bandwidth and can arrive with bands out of order
(seen with a webcam passed through to a virtual machine).
Requires: opencv-python (``uv sync --extra camera``) and a webcam, or
--simulate, which uses a moving test picture and the simulated controller.
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
import time

import cv2
from roi_view import RoiSelector, synthetic_frame

from arena_interface import Device


def open_camera(index: int, width: int, height: int) -> cv2.VideoCapture:
    """Open a webcam asking for MJPG frames of the given size at 30 fps."""
    camera = cv2.VideoCapture(index)
    camera.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FOURCC, cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"MJPG"))  # before size
    camera.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_WIDTH, width)
    camera.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_HEIGHT, height)
    camera.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS, 30)
    return camera


def hide_native_warnings() -> None:
    """Drop C-library messages (e.g. libjpeg's harmless "Corrupt JPEG data").

    Many Logitech webcams trigger one per frame. Python's own errors still
    show: sys.stderr is moved to a copy of the original stream first.
    """
    sys.stderr = os.fdopen(os.dup(2), "w", buffering=1)
    os.dup2(os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY), 2)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--simulate", action="store_true", help="fake device and test picture"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--camera", type=int, default=0, help="camera number")
    parser.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=640, help="camera image width")
    parser.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=480, help="camera image height")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, help="stop after this long")
    parser.add_argument("--gs2", action="store_true", help="start in GS2 (dithered)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mirror",
        action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
        default=True,
        help="mirror left-right (default: on)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--rotate", type=float, default=0.0, help="shift around the arena, 0-360 deg"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--brightness", type=int, default=128, help="panel duty cycle 1-255"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--no-gui", action="store_true", help="no windows")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    camera = None
    if not args.simulate:
        camera = open_camera(args.camera, args.width, args.height)
        if not camera.isOpened():
            parser.error(f"cannot open camera {args.camera}")
        hide_native_warnings()

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        roi = RoiSelector(
            dev.arena.pixel_shape,
            gui=not args.no_gui,
            gs2=args.gs2,
            mirror=args.mirror,
            rotate=args.rotate,
            brightness=args.brightness,
        )
        start, sent = time.monotonic(), 0
        try:
            while roi.poll():
                elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
                if args.seconds is not None and elapsed >= args.seconds:
                    break
                if camera is None:  # a 30 fps "camera"
                    time.sleep(max(0.0, start + sent / 30 - time.monotonic()))
                    frame = synthetic_frame(elapsed)
                else:
                    ok, frame = camera.read()  # waits for the next camera frame
                    if not ok:
                        raise SystemExit("the camera stopped delivering frames")
                dev.stream_image(
                    roi.update(frame),
                    gray_level=roi.gray_level,
                    duty_cycle=roi.brightness,
                )
                sent += 1
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            roi.close()
            if camera is not None:
                camera.release()
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
        print(f"sent {sent} frames in {elapsed:.1f} s ({sent / elapsed:.1f} fps)")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The same for a movie file (.mp4, .avi, .gif, ...), played at its own frame rate with dev.pace().

uv run python examples/camera/movie.py clip.mp4

"""Play a movie file (.mp4, .avi, .gif, ...) on the arena through a box you move.

Shows: reading frames with OpenCV, dev.pace() keeping the movie's own frame
rate (skipping frames if the computer falls behind), and the same
crop -> shrink -> dev.stream_image() path as webcam.py. Space pauses (the box
still moves); the movie loops unless --once. See roi_view.py for the mouse and
keyboard controls.
Requires: opencv-python (``uv sync --extra camera``) and a movie file; with
--simulate and no file, a moving test picture and the simulated controller.
"""

import argparse
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
from roi_view import RoiSelector, synthetic_frame

from arena_interface import Device


def next_frame(video: cv2.VideoCapture, skip: int, loop: bool):
    """The next frame after skipping `skip` (None at the end without --loop)."""
    for _ in range(skip):
        video.grab()
    ok, frame = video.read()
    if not ok and loop:
        video.set(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_FRAMES, 0)
        ok, frame = video.read()
    return frame if ok else None


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("movie", nargs="?", type=Path, help="movie file")
    parser.add_argument("--port", help="serial port (default: auto-detect)")
    parser.add_argument("--simulate", action="store_true", help="use fake device")
    parser.add_argument("--speed", type=float, default=1.0, help="playback speed")
    parser.add_argument("--once", action="store_true", help="do not loop")
    parser.add_argument("--seconds", type=float, help="stop after this long")
    parser.add_argument("--gs2", action="store_true", help="start in GS2 (dithered)")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--mirror",
        action=argparse.BooleanOptionalAction,
        default=False,
        help="mirror left-right (default: off)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--rotate", type=float, default=0.0, help="shift around the arena, 0-360 deg"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--brightness", type=int, default=128, help="panel duty cycle 1-255"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--no-gui", action="store_true", help="no windows")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    video, fps = None, 30.0
    if args.movie is not None:
        video = cv2.VideoCapture(str(args.movie))
        if not video.isOpened():
            parser.error(f"cannot open {args.movie}")
        fps = video.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_FPS) or fps
    elif not args.simulate:
        parser.error("give a movie file (or --simulate for a test picture)")

    with Device.open(args.port, simulate=args.simulate) as dev:
        roi = RoiSelector(
            dev.arena.pixel_shape,
            gui=not args.no_gui,
            gs2=args.gs2,
            mirror=args.mirror,
            rotate=args.rotate,
            brightness=args.brightness,
        )
        pacer = dev.pace(fps * args.speed, duration=args.seconds, late="skip")
        frame = None
        try:
            for tick in pacer:
                if not roi.poll():
                    break
                if frame is None or not roi.paused:
                    if video is None:
                        frame = synthetic_frame(tick.index / fps)
                    else:
                        frame = next_frame(video, tick.skipped, loop=not args.once)
                    if frame is None:
                        break
                dev.stream_image(
                    roi.update(frame),
                    gray_level=roi.gray_level,
                    duty_cycle=roi.brightness,
                )
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            pass
        finally:
            roi.close()
            if video is not None:
                video.release()
        print(f"{fps * args.speed:g} frames/s: {pacer.report}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

The box and the preview window shared by both camera examples, with the mouse and keyboard controls in its docstring.

"""Shared helper for the camera examples: a box you move over the video.

Not an example on its own; ``webcam.py`` and ``movie.py`` import it. The box
keeps the arena's aspect ratio (5:1 on a 2x10 arena). What is inside it is
shrunk to the arena's pixel size, optionally rotated around the arena, and
shown, as the panels will show it, in a second window.

Controls (click the "source" window first so it has the keyboard):

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| drag inside the box | move it |
| click outside the box | centre it there (keep holding to drag) |
| drag a corner | resize it (the opposite corner stays put) |
| mouse wheel, ``+`` / ``-`` | resize about the centre |
| arrow keys, ``w`` ``a`` ``s`` ``d`` | move the box (2% of the picture height) |
| ``r`` | reset to the largest centred box |
| ``m`` | mirror left-right |
| ``g`` | switch GS16 / GS2 (dithered) |
| ``c`` | contrast stretch on/off |
| ``[`` / ``]`` | rotate around the arena (5 columns, 9 degrees on a 2x10 arena) |
| ``,`` / ``.`` | dim / brighten the panels (duty cycle 1-255, x1.25 per press) |
| space | pause (movie.py) |
| ``q`` or Esc | quit |

Requires: opencv-python (``uv sync --extra camera``).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

import cv2
import numpy as np

from arena_interface import GrayLevel

SOURCE_WINDOW = "source"
ARENA_WINDOW = "arena"
MAX_DISPLAY_WIDTH = 960  # larger videos are shown scaled down
CORNER_GRAB = 12  # display pixels around a corner that start a resize
MIN_BOX_WIDTH = 20  # source pixels
ROTATE_STEP_COLUMNS = 5  # arena columns per [ or ] key press
BOX_COLOR = (0, 255, 0)  # BGR
CONTROLS = """\
In the source window: drag the box (or use the arrow keys or w a s d) to move
it; drag a corner (or use the mouse wheel or + / -) to resize it.
Keys: r reset, m mirror, g GS16/GS2, c contrast, [ ] rotate,
, . dim/brighten, space pause, q quit."""
MOVE_STEP = 0.02  # fraction of the picture height per key press
# Arrow-key codes from cv2.waitKeyEx(): Linux, Windows, macOS.
_ARROWS = {
    **dict.fromkeys((65361, 2424832, 63234), (-1, 0)),  # left
    **dict.fromkeys((65362, 2490368, 63232), (0, -1)),  # up
    **dict.fromkeys((65363, 2555904, 63235), (1, 0)),  # right
    **dict.fromkeys((65364, 2621440, 63233), (0, 1)),  # down
}
# 4x4 Bayer matrix: thresholds for ordered dithering in GS2.
_BAYER4 = (
    np.array([[0, 8, 2, 10], [12, 4, 14, 6], [3, 11, 1, 9], [15, 7, 13, 5]]) + 0.5
) / 16


def to_arena_image(
    crop: np.ndarray, shape: tuple[int, int], *, gs2: bool = False, stretch: bool = True
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Turn a BGR crop into an arena image: 0-15 (GS16) or dithered 0/1 (GS2)."""
    h, w = shape
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(crop, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY) if crop.ndim == 3 else crop
    small = cv2.resize(gray, (w, h), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA).astype(np.float32)
    if stretch:  # use the full brightness range: 16 levels go a long way
        lo, hi = np.percentile(small, (2, 98))
        level = (small - lo) / max(hi - lo, 1.0)
    else:
        level = small / 255
    level = np.clip(level, 0.0, 1.0)
    if gs2:
        threshold = np.tile(_BAYER4, (h // 4 + 1, w // 4 + 1))[:h, :w]
        return (level > threshold).astype(np.uint8)
    return np.round(level * 15).astype(np.uint8)


def synthetic_frame(t: float, size: tuple[int, int] = (640, 480)) -> np.ndarray:
    """A moving test picture (BGR) standing in for a camera or a movie."""
    w, h = size
    bars = (127 + 120 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * (np.arange(w) / 80 - t / 2))).astype(
        np.uint8
    )
    frame = np.repeat(np.tile(bars, (h, 1))[:, :, None], 3, axis=2)
    centre = (int(w / 2 + w / 3 * np.cos(t)), int(h / 2 + h / 4 * np.sin(2 * t)))
    cv2.circle(frame, centre, 40, (0, 0, 255), -1)
    return frame


class RoiSelector:
    """A box of fixed aspect ratio over the video, moved with the mouse.

    Args:
        arena_shape: ``(height, width)`` of the arena image, e.g.
            ``dev.arena.pixel_shape``.
        gui: Show the windows and take mouse/keyboard input.
        gs2: Start in GS2 (dithered on/off) instead of GS16.
        mirror: Flip the video left-right (natural for a webcam facing you).
        rotate: Move the image's centre around the arena by this many degrees
            (0-360; 360 is the full image width, back to the start).
        brightness: Panel brightness (duty cycle) 1-255; 128 is 50 %.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        arena_shape: tuple[int, int],
        *,
        gui: bool = True,
        gs2: bool = False,
        mirror: bool = False,
        rotate: float = 0.0,
        brightness: int = 128,
    ) -> None:
        """Set up the box (sized on the first frame) and the windows."""
        self.arena_shape = arena_shape
        self.aspect = arena_shape[1] / arena_shape[0]  # width / height
        self.gui, self.gs2, self.mirror = gui, gs2, mirror
        self.rotate = rotate
        if not 1 <= brightness <= 255:
            raise ValueError(f"brightness must be 1-255, got {brightness}")
        self.brightness = brightness
        """Duty cycle to send the images with (``dev.stream_image(duty_cycle=)``)."""
        self.stretch = True
        self.paused = False
        self.box = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)  # x, y, width in source pixels
        self._frame_size = (0, 0)
        self._scale = 1.0  # display pixels per source pixel
        self._drag: tuple[str, float, float] | None = None
        self._fps = 0.0
        self._last = time.monotonic()
        if gui:
            cv2.namedWindow(SOURCE_WINDOW, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
            cv2.namedWindow(ARENA_WINDOW, cv2.WINDOW_AUTOSIZE)
            cv2.setMouseCallback(SOURCE_WINDOW, self._on_mouse)
            print(CONTROLS)

    @property
    def gray_level(self) -> GrayLevel:
        """Gray level to send the images with."""
        return GrayLevel.GS2 if self.gs2 else GrayLevel.GS16

    def update(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Crop the box from a BGR frame and return the arena image (and show it)."""
        if self.mirror:
            frame = np.ascontiguousarray(frame[:, ::-1])
        fh, fw = frame.shape[:2]
        if (fw, fh) != self._frame_size:
            self._frame_size = (fw, fh)
            self._scale = min(1.0, MAX_DISPLAY_WIDTH / fw)
            self.reset()
        x, y, w = (round(v) for v in self.box)
        crop = frame[y : y + round(w / self.aspect), x : x + w]
        image = to_arena_image(
            crop, self.arena_shape, gs2=self.gs2, stretch=self.stretch
        )
        shift = round(self.rotate % 360 / 360 * image.shape[1])
        image = np.roll(image, shift, axis=1)  # columns wrap around the arena
        now = time.monotonic()
        self._fps = 0.9 * self._fps + 0.1 / max(now - self._last, 1e-6)
        self._last = now
        if self.gui:
            self._show(frame, image)
        return image

    def poll(self) -> bool:
        """Handle key presses; False once the user quits (always True with no GUI)."""
        if not self.gui:
            return True
        code = cv2.waitKeyEx(1)
        if code in _ARROWS:
            self._move(*_ARROWS[code])
            return True
        key = code & 0xFF
        if key in (ord("q"), 27):
            return False
        actions = {
            ord("r"): self.reset,
            ord("m"): lambda: setattr(self, "mirror", not self.mirror),
            ord("g"): lambda: setattr(self, "gs2", not self.gs2),
            ord("c"): lambda: setattr(self, "stretch", not self.stretch),
            ord(","): lambda: self._dim(1 / 1.25),
            ord("."): lambda: self._dim(1.25),
            ord("["): lambda: self._turn(-1),
            ord("]"): lambda: self._turn(+1),
            ord(" "): lambda: setattr(self, "paused", not self.paused),
            ord("+"): lambda: self._zoom(1.1),
            ord("="): lambda: self._zoom(1.1),
            ord("-"): lambda: self._zoom(1 / 1.1),
            ord("w"): lambda: self._move(0, -1),
            ord("a"): lambda: self._move(-1, 0),
            ord("s"): lambda: self._move(0, 1),
            ord("d"): lambda: self._move(1, 0),
        }
        if key in actions:
            actions[key]()
        # Closing the window with its title-bar button also quits.
        return cv2.getWindowProperty(SOURCE_WINDOW, cv2.WND_PROP_VISIBLE) >= 1

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the windows."""
        if self.gui:
            cv2.destroyAllWindows()

    # -- the box ------------------------------------------------------------

    def reset(self) -> None:
        """The largest box that fits, centred."""
        fw, fh = self._frame_size
        w = min(fw, fh * self.aspect)
        self.box = ((fw - w) / 2, (fh - w / self.aspect) / 2, w)

    def _place(self, x: float, y: float, w: float) -> None:
        """Set the box, limiting its size and keeping it inside the frame."""
        fw, fh = self._frame_size
        w = min(max(w, MIN_BOX_WIDTH), fw, fh * self.aspect)
        h = w / self.aspect
        self.box = (min(max(x, 0.0), fw - w), min(max(y, 0.0), fh - h), w)

    def _move(self, dx: int, dy: int) -> None:
        step = MOVE_STEP * self._frame_size[1]
        x, y, w = self.box
        self._place(x + dx * step, y + dy * step, w)

    def _dim(self, factor: float) -> None:
        b = self.brightness
        step = round(b * factor) - b
        if step == 0:  # always move by at least one at the low end
            step = 1 if factor > 1 else -1
        self.brightness = min(max(b + step, 1), 255)

    def _turn(self, direction: int) -> None:
        step = 360 * ROTATE_STEP_COLUMNS / self.arena_shape[1]
        self.rotate = (self.rotate + direction * step) % 360

    def _zoom(self, factor: float) -> None:
        x, y, w = self.box
        cx, cy = x + w / 2, y + w / self.aspect / 2
        fw, fh = self._frame_size
        w = min(max(w * factor, MIN_BOX_WIDTH), fw, fh * self.aspect)
        self._place(cx - w / 2, cy - w / self.aspect / 2, w)

    def _on_mouse(self, event: int, x: int, y: int, flags: int, _param: object) -> None:
        sx, sy = x / self._scale, y / self._scale  # source pixels
        bx, by, bw = self.box
        bh = bw / self.aspect
        if event == cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONDOWN:
            corners = [(bx, by), (bx + bw, by), (bx, by + bh), (bx + bw, by + bh)]
            grab = CORNER_GRAB / self._scale
            for i, (cx, cy) in enumerate(corners):
                if abs(sx - cx) <= grab and abs(sy - cy) <= grab:
                    self._drag = ("resize", *corners[3 - i])  # anchor: opposite
                    return
            if not (bx <= sx <= bx + bw and by <= sy <= by + bh):
                self._place(sx - bw / 2, sy - bh / 2, bw)
                bx, by, _ = self.box
            self._drag = ("move", sx - bx, sy - by)
        elif event == cv2.EVENT_MOUSEMOVE and self._drag is not None:
            kind, a, b = self._drag
            if kind == "move":
                self._place(sx - a, sy - b, bw)
            else:  # resize from anchor (a, b) towards the pointer
                # Size from the pointer's offset projected on the box's
                # diagonal, so dragging mostly sideways resizes a wide box.
                dx, dy = abs(sx - a), abs(sy - b)
                w = (dx * self.aspect + dy) / (self.aspect**2 + 1) * self.aspect
                w = max(w, MIN_BOX_WIDTH)
                h = w / self.aspect
                self._place(a if sx >= a else a - w, b if sy >= b else b - h, w)
        elif event == cv2.EVENT_LBUTTONUP:
            self._drag = None
        elif event == cv2.EVENT_MOUSEWHEEL:
            # The wheel step is the signed top 16 bits of flags (OpenCV 5 has
            # no getMouseWheelDelta); positive means away from the user.
            delta = (flags >> 16) & 0xFFFF
            self._zoom(1 / 1.1 if delta >= 0x8000 else 1.1)

    # -- display ------------------------------------------------------------

    def _show(self, frame: np.ndarray, image: np.ndarray) -> None:
        s = self._scale
        view = (
            cv2.resize(frame, None, fx=s, fy=s, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
            if s < 1
            else frame.copy()
        )
        x, y, w = self.box
        h = w / self.aspect
        p1 = (round(x * s), round(y * s))
        p2 = (round((x + w) * s) - 1, round((y + h) * s) - 1)
        cv2.rectangle(view, p1, p2, BOX_COLOR, 2)
        status = "  ".join(
            [
                "GS2" if self.gs2 else "GS16",
                f"rotate {self.rotate % 360:.0f} deg",
                f"brightness {self.brightness}",
                f"stretch {'on' if self.stretch else 'off'}",
                *(["PAUSED"] if self.paused else []),
                f"{self._fps:.0f} fps",
            ]
        )
        for color, thickness in (((0, 0, 0), 3), ((255, 255, 255), 1)):
            cv2.putText(
                view, status, (8, 22), cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.6, color, thickness
            )
        cv2.imshow(SOURCE_WINDOW, view)
        # The arena as green LEDs, enlarged with square pixels.
        zoom = max(1, 800 // image.shape[1])
        levels = 1 if self.gs2 else 15
        green = (image.astype(np.uint32) * self.brightness // levels).astype(np.uint8)
        green = cv2.resize(
            green, None, fx=zoom, fy=zoom, interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST
        )
        dark = np.zeros_like(green)
        cv2.imshow(ARENA_WINDOW, cv2.merge([dark, green, dark]))

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
The library is installed from a copy of this repository.

uvpip 
uv sync                          # creates .venv with the library and dev tools

To use it from another uv project:

uv add /path/to/arena-interface

pip install /path/to/arena-interface

The dependencies, pyserial and numpy, are installed automatically.

docs.title: Allow access to the serial port
docs.text:
LinuxmacOSWindows

The controller appears as /dev/ttyACM0 (or ttyACM1, ...). Your user needs permission to open it:

  1. Install the Teensy udev rules from PJRC, which also stop ModemManager from grabbing the port:

    curl -fsSL https://www.pjrc.com/teensy/00-teensy.rules -o /tmp/00-teensy.rules
sudo cp /tmp/00-teensy.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger

  2. Unplug and replug the controller.

If you still get "permission denied", add yourself to the dialout group (sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER) and log out and back in.

No setup is needed. The controller appears as /dev/cu.usbmodem....

No setup is needed on Windows 10 and later. The controller appears as a COM port.

Only one program can use the port at a time: close serial monitors, the web console or other scripts first.

docs.title: Connect
docs.text:
from arena_interface import Device

with Device.open() as dev:
    print(dev.firmware_version)
    print(dev.arena)              # the panel grid, e.g. G6_2x10
    print(dev.arena.pixel_shape)  # image size for patterns, e.g. (40, 200)

Device.open() without arguments finds the controller by its USB ids. If several Teensy boards are connected, it asks each one whether it is a controller. To skip detection, pass the port name: Device.open("/dev/ttyACM0") or Device.open("COM5"). To see what is connected:

from arena_interface import find_ports

for port in find_ports():
    print(port.device, port.description)

Leaving the with block blanks the arena and releases the port. Use Device.open(..., all_off_on_close=False) to leave the display running.

docs.title: Try it without hardware
docs.text:
Every part of the library works against a simulated controller:

with Device.open(simulate=True) as dev:
    dev.start_trial(1, frame_rate=30)
    print(dev.frame_position)

The simulator starts with two demo patterns on its SD card. All examples accept --simulate:

uv run python examples/01_connect.py --simulate
uv run python examples/06_trials.py               # the real controller

        print(entry.pattern_id, entry.name)

    dev.start_trial(1, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=30, duration=3)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause DeviceNotFound: no G6 arena controller found Cable unplugged, or the port is not visible to the OS. Run find_ports(all_ports=True) to see every port. DeviceNotFound: cannot open ...: Permission denied Port permissions (see above). DeviceNotFound: cannot open ...: ... busy Another program has the port open. DeviceTimeout on every command The port is not a controller, or the controller is wedged; reset it or replug the cable. A brief "CE NN" glyph on the arena The controller rejected a command. The library prevents most cases; see Errors.

docs.title: User guide
docs.text: This guide explains how the controller works and how each part of the library maps onto it. Every name used here is importable from arena_interface.

docs.title: How the controller works
docs.text:
The controller drives a grid of 20 × 20-pixel LED panels from a Teensy 4.1. Each firmware build is compiled for one grid (2 × 10, 4 × 10 or 4 × 12 panels); the library reads it when connecting: dev.arena is that grid as an Arena (e.g. the G6_2x10 preset), and dev.arena.pixel_shape is the image size for patterns.

The controller is always in one state (ArenaState):

State Started by What the arena shows ALL_OFF all_off(), stop(), end of a timed trial, after an error Dark ALL_ON all_on() Every pixel at full brightness OPEN_LOOP start_trial(..., TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP) A pattern advancing at a frame rate SHOW_FRAME show_pattern(), show_frame(), start_trial(..., TrialMode.SHOW_FRAME) The frame you choose CLOSED_LOOP start_trial(..., TrialMode.CLOSED_LOOP) A pattern whose speed follows Analog In 1 STREAMING_FRAME stream_frame(), stream_image() A frame sent from the computer PSRAM_PLAY show_panel_frame(), play_panel_frames() Frames stored in the panels themselves ERROR_DISPLAY A rejected command A "CE NN" error code for 0.75 s, then dark

The controller only ever answers commands; it never sends anything on its own. Everything "live" in this library (event streams, sampling) is the computer asking repeatedly.

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
from arena_interface import Device

dev = Device.open()                  # auto-detect
dev = Device.open("/dev/ttyACM0")    # a specific port; no detection
dev = Device.open(simulate=True)     # the simulated controller

Auto-detection looks for USB serial ports with the Teensy's ids (16C0:0483). Any Teensy has these ids, so when several match, the library asks each one for its controller information and keeps the one that answers as a G6 controller (probe=False turns that off and makes several matches an error). find_ports() lists candidates without sending anything.

When connecting, the library reads the controller's identity:

dev.info.mac                # unique per controller
dev.firmware                # FirmwareVersion: git SHA, build date, grid, flags
dev.capabilities            # Capability flags
dev.supports(Capability.IO_EXT)

docs.title: Closing
docs.text: Close with a with block or dev.close(). Closing sends ALL_OFF first so the arena goes dark: the controller otherwise keeps displaying after the computer disconnects. Pass all_off_on_close=False (or set the attribute) to leave a stimulus running. Closing never raises, even if the device has already gone.

docs.title: Reset and reconnect
docs.text: dev.reset() reboots the controller; the USB connection drops and the device object is closed. dev.reconnect() waits (10 s by default) for the same controller to come back, checked by its MAC address, so a different controller on the same port is not picked up by mistake. reconnect() also recovers after a DeviceDisconnected error (cable unplugged).

docs.title: Displaying patterns from the SD card
docs.text:
Patterns on the SD card are addressed by a 1-based id in alphabetical order of file name.

dev.start_trial(3, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=60)      # forwards
dev.start_trial(3, TrialMode.OPEN_LOOP, frame_rate=-60)     # backwards
dev.start_trial(3, TrialMode.CLOSED_LOOP, gain=20)          # 2 fps per volt
dev.start_trial(3, frame_rate=60, duration=5.0)             # stops by itself
dev.start_trial(3, frame_rate=60, duty_cycle=64)            # dimmer, this trial only

duration is timed by the controller (10 ms resolution, up to 655 s), so the trial ends on time even if the computer is busy. duty_cycle overrides the brightness stored in the pattern for this trial only.

To choose each frame yourself:

dev.show_pattern(3)                 # load, show frame 0, don't advance
for i in range(dev.frame_position.frame_count):
    dev.show_frame(i)

show_frame checks the index locally, because an out-of-range index would make the controller show an error code and stop the display.

docs.title: Patterns from pixel arrays
docs.text:
A Pattern is one image per frame covering the whole arena: rows * 20 pixels high, cols * 20 wide, which is dev.arena.pixel_shape for the connected controller.

from arena_interface import Pattern, GrayLevel

h, w = dev.arena.pixel_shape                      # e.g. (40, 200) for 2x10
frames = [[[15 if (x + f) % 40 < 20 else 0 for x in range(w)] for _ in range(h)]
          for f in range(40)]
pattern = Pattern.from_frames(frames, gray_level=GrayLevel.GS16, arena=dev.arena)

pattern_id = dev.patterns.upload("stripes.pat", pattern)
dev.start_trial(pattern_id, frame_rate=40)
  • Gray levels: GrayLevel.GS2 takes 0/1 (or booleans), GrayLevel.GS16 takes 0-15.
  • Orientation: row 0 is the top of the arena (origin="upper", as in numpy and matplotlib). Data whose row 0 is the bottom, as in the MATLAB and JavaScript tools, needs origin="lower". Columns run left to right.
  • Brightness: duty_cycle (1-255, default 128) for all frames or one per frame.
  • Arrays: frames can be 2-D numpy arrays, nested lists, or one 3-D array (frames, height, width), with any integer or boolean dtype. pattern.frame(i) returns one frame as a (height, width) uint8 array and pattern.to_numpy() all of them as (frames, height, width).
  • Files: pattern.to_bytes() gives the .pat file; Pattern.from_bytes() reads one (checking every checksum).

docs.title: Arenas, partial arenas and fitting
docs.text:
Arena describes a rig. The arenas in the maDisplayTools registry are built in:

from arena_interface import Arena, PRESETS

Arena.preset("G6_2x8of10")    # 2x10 grid, columns 1-8 installed
list(PRESETS)                 # all preset names

Partial-arena presets such as G6_3x12of18 describe arenas built with a permanent cut-out, for example for access when used with a 2-photon microscope. Draw a partial arena's images on its full grid; columns without panels are ignored.

Temporarily removed panels

Panels or whole columns taken out for a while, to make room for other instruments, do not make an arena partial. Keep using the full arena (or no arena= at all): the library always sends data for every panel position, so the remaining panels display correctly and a replaced panel works again with no change on the computer.

A rig can also be smaller than the grid its controller firmware was built for (a 3 × 10 rig on 4 × 10 firmware, or G6_3x12of18 on 4 × 12). The library then fits the image to the firmware's grid: grid column c goes to firmware column c, and the rig's rows are repeated up the frame so the panels light whichever row connector they are on.

rig = Arena.preset("G6_3x10")
pattern = Pattern.from_frames(frames, arena=rig)
dev.patterns.upload("rig.pat", pattern)          # fitted automatically
fitted = pattern.fit_to(4, 10)                     # or explicitly

The controller refuses any .pat file whose grid differs from its own; the library checks this before uploading.

docs.title: The SD-card pattern library
docs.text:
len(dev.patterns)                          # how many
for entry in dev.patterns:                 # PatternEntry(pattern_id, name)
    print(entry.pattern_id, entry.name)
dev.patterns.info(3)                       # frames, gray level, grid, size
data = dev.patterns.download(3)            # the .pat file
new_id = dev.patterns.upload("x.pat", data_or_pattern, overwrite=True)
new_id = dev.patterns.rename(new_id, "y.pat")
dev.patterns.delete(new_id)
zip_bytes = dev.patterns.archive()         # the whole card as a ZIP
dev.patterns.format_card()                 # erases everything

Note

Ids are positions in alphabetical order, so uploading, renaming and deleting can change the ids of other patterns. The methods that change the library return the new id; look ids up with patterns.find(name) rather than storing them for long.

Downloading, uploading, archiving and formatting need the display to be off: call dev.stop() first, otherwise the controller refuses with a CommandError.

docs.title: Streaming frames from the computer
docs.text:
stream_image() displays one image immediately, without the SD card:

dev.stream_image(image, gray_level=GrayLevel.GS2)
dev.stream_image(rig_image, arena=Arena.preset("G6_3x10"))   # fitted

stream_frame(payload) sends a frame payload you encoded yourself (pattern.stream_payload(i)). Each frame is one USB transfer of 1-10 KB, depending on the arena size and gray level. To send frames at a fixed rate, use host-paced playback (next section).

Frames can also live in the panels' own memory: show_panel_frame(i) and play_panel_frames(start, count, fps).

docs.title: Host-paced playback
docs.text:
Here the computer decides when each frame is shown, either from a sequence prepared in advance or chosen live, for example from a tracking system.

dev.show_pattern(4)
report = dev.play_frames(range(200), fps=200)              # frames of an SD pattern
report = dev.play_images(images, fps=120)                  # streamed images
print(report)    # e.g. "200/200 frames at 200/s in 1.00 s; skipped 0, late 0; ..."

In the background. start_frames() and start_images() take the same arguments and return a Playback while the frames play in a separate thread:

with dev.start_frames(range(200), fps=200) as player:
    while player.running:
        print(player.progress, "of", player.total)   # your script keeps working
        time.sleep(0.1)
report = player.report       # or player.wait() / player.stop()

Your script may keep using the device meanwhile; each of its commands delays the next frame slightly, and the report shows the effect. wait() re-raises any error the playback hit (for example DeviceDisconnected).

Live (closed loop). pace() is a fixed-rate clock; send whatever frame you choose on each tick:

pacer = dev.pace(200, duration=10)
for tick in pacer:
    dev.show_frame(frame_from_tracker())     # or dev.stream_image(...)
print(pacer.report)

Each Tick has its slot number, due time and lateness; tick.skipped says how many slots were skipped just before it, so you can catch up.

docs.title: Timing and late frames
docs.text:
Frames are scheduled against a fixed clock, so errors do not accumulate. The scheduler sleeps until just before each slot and then waits the last fraction of a millisecond actively, which gives sub-millisecond timing on Linux, macOS and Windows (Python 3.11+).

When a frame cannot be sent on time (the computer or the controller was busy), late="skip" (the default) drops frames whose slot has passed, so the sequence keeps its schedule and length; late="send" sends every frame, possibly late, so the sequence runs long. Either way:

  • the PlaybackReport gives frames sent, skipped and late (more than half a frame period after their slot), and median, 99th-percentile and worst lateness;
  • falling behind is logged on arena_interface.playback (at most one line per second);
  • play_frames(..., verify=True) reads the controller's log afterwards and reports how many frame changes actually reached the panels (displayed, to compare with changes) and how many were replaced unseen.

docs.title: How fast?
docs.text:
A frame is displayed only if it stays in place for at least one refresh of the controller (dev.refresh_rate), so keep fps below the refresh rate; a PerformanceWarning is issued if it is too close. On a 2x10 arena the refresh rate defaults to 300 Hz for GS16 content and 1000 Hz for GS2. Pass refresh_rate= to the playback functions to raise it first, but note that a refresh rate set from the computer stays in force (for all content) until the controller restarts, and that the panels themselves redraw at 1 kHz.

Frames of an SD pattern also wait for the controller to read them from the card. That usually takes under 2 ms but occasionally stalls, so close to the refresh rate a frame can now and then be replaced unseen; verify=True shows it. Measured limits are in the protocol reference.

docs.title: Display settings
docs.text:
dev.refresh_rate                 # Hz at which the frame is re-sent to the panels
dev.refresh_rate = 500           # stays in force until the controller restarts
dev.panel_display_mode           # PanelDisplayMode: ONESHOT, PERSIST, TRIGGERED, GATED
dev.frames_sent                  # frames pushed to the panels; reset_frames_sent()

docs.title: Analog and digital I/O
docs.text:
io = dev.io
io.analog_out = 2500                         # mV, 0-5000; reads back from the DAC
io.load_analog_table([0, 2500, 5000])        # follows the frame index (1-21 levels)
io.set_analog_out_mode(AoMode.FRAME_NUMBER)  # 0 V first frame .. 5 V last frame
io.read_analog_in()                          # AnalogInputs(ain1_mv, ain2_mv), uncalibrated

io.dio_roles()                               # roles and levels of ports 1 and 2
io.set_dio_role(1, DioRole.OUT_PROGRAMMABLE)
io.set_digital_out(1, True)
io.read_digital()

Port 2 starts as the external-trigger input for the triggered and gated panel modes; the controller refuses to drive it until its role is changed. The analog inputs are not calibrated in firmware; example 23 shows a loopback calibration.

docs.title: Telemetry: what the arena actually displayed
docs.text:
The controller logs every command it receives, every change of the displayed frame and every state change, with microsecond timestamps, in a ring buffer that survives software resets.

from arena_interface import FrameRecord

dev.telemetry.drain()                              # discard older events
dev.start_trial(1, frame_rate=60, duration=2)
for event in dev.telemetry.events(duration=2.2):
    if isinstance(event.record, FrameRecord):
        print(event.time, event.record.index)
  • event.time is wall-clock time (time.time()) of the controller's own timestamp, so it is more accurate than timing on the computer. event.record.t_us is the raw controller time.
  • Records are only removed from the controller after they have been returned to you. Breaking out of a loop and starting another neither loses nor repeats events.
  • Records written before the controller's last reset have time=None.
  • Events lost because the ring overflowed are counted (stream.lost, dev.telemetry.lost) and logged.
  • Times stay correct for records hours old: each record is dated from the next newer one. The controller's microsecond clock wraps every 71.6 minutes, so if it logged nothing for longer than that, the gap is ambiguous. The library resolves it from the controller's uptime when the boot record is among the records read; otherwise records before such a gap can be dated 71.6 minutes (or a multiple) too late.

docs.title: Sampling at a fixed rate
docs.text:
dev.sample() calls any reading at a fixed rate:

for s in dev.sample(dev.io.read_analog_in, rate_hz=100, duration=10):
    print(s.time, s.value.ain1_mv)

The schedule does not drift; readings that cannot keep up are skipped and counted (sampler.skipped). Each reading is one USB round trip of about 1 ms, so a few hundred readings per second is the practical limit.

docs.title: Diagnostics and panel firmware
docs.text:
dev.diagnostics has the controller's health counters (uptime, loop and SD timing, and what the previous boot was doing when it last reset), the last CPU fault, SD card identity, debug-text output and the panel SPI clock.

dev.panel_firmware stores a panel firmware image on the SD card, then programs and verifies panels one at a time (1-based panel numbers, as on the panel map). The display must be off.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All exceptions derive from DeviceError.

Exception Meaning What to do CommandError The controller refused a command. .status and .message say why. Check the message; ErrorCode.DISPLAY_ACTIVE means stop the display first. UnsupportedCommand The firmware does not advertise this feature. Nothing was sent. Check dev.supports(...) first, or update the firmware. DeviceTimeout No answer in time. Also a TimeoutError. Retry; if it persists, reset or replug. DeviceDisconnected The connection was lost; the device is now closed. dev.reconnect(). DeviceNotFound No controller found, or the port could not be opened. See troubleshooting. ProtocolError The device sent malformed data. Report it; usually a firmware mismatch.

Invalid arguments (a frame index out of range, a pattern with the wrong size) raise ValueError or TypeError before anything is sent. The library checks the cases that would otherwise make the controller show an error code and stop the display.

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text: Ordinary commands wait 1 s for an answer. Slower commands get longer limits: SD-card operations 30 s, programming or verifying a panel 60 s, and formatting the card 180 s. Bulk transfers (pattern and archive downloads) fail if no data arrives for 5 s.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text: A Device may be shared between threads. Each method is atomic: the wire protocol allows one request at a time, and the device serialises them, so a thread just waits while another's request is in progress. Multi-step methods (such as patterns.upload) hold the lock for their whole sequence. A sequence of calls in your own code is not atomic; use your own lock if another thread must not interleave. Event streams and samplers release the lock between polls, so other threads can send commands while they run.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
The library logs through the standard logging module:

Logger Level Content arena_interface.transport DEBUG Every byte sent and received arena_interface.transport WARNING Late replies to earlier requests, skipped arena_interface.framing WARNING Bytes from the device that were not a valid frame arena_interface.firmware INFO Debug text printed by debug firmware builds arena_interface.streaming WARNING Lost telemetry records 
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)
logging.getLogger("arena_interface.transport").setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

docs.title: Testing your own code
docs.text:
Device.open(simulate=True) connects to a FakeController, which emulates the firmware: the same replies, error codes and side effects, an in-memory SD card, the telemetry log and the I/O state. Pass your own controller to configure it or to inject faults:

from arena_interface.testing import FakeController, make_test_pattern

ctrl = FakeController(rows=4, cols=10, patterns={"a.pat": make_test_pattern(4, 10)})
with Device.open(simulate=ctrl) as dev:
    ctrl.analog_in = (1500, -200)          # what the inputs read
    ctrl.unplug()                          # the next command raises DeviceDisconnected

dev.simulator gives access to the controller of a simulated device. The simulator does not render pixels.
